# Use Auto Payments with settlement accounts

Source: https://docs.tink.com/resources/auto-payments/use-auto-payments-with-settlement-accounts.md

# Use Auto Payments with settlement accounts

Manage pay-ins, payouts and reconciliation across your organization or merchant network. 

## Prerequisites

1. To use settlement accounts in sandbox or production, contact [Support](https://support.tink.com) or your Account Manager.
2. You've read and completed the prerequisites for “Initiate your first Auto Payment” initiated your first one-time payment. 
3. You've enabled settlement accounts and the following scopes: `settlement-accounts` and, `settlement-accounts:readonly` and `payment:write`. 

## What is a settlement account? 

Settlement Accounts are virtual bank accounts that are set up and managed by Tink. The accounts provide aggregated settlements, which enables features like real-time payment status updates, refunds and withdrawals, automated reconciliation and integrated reporting. 

You can set up a single account or set up multiple accounts for specific business units or use cases. Accounts can be configured and interacted with through either [Console](/resources/console.md) or a direct integration with our [Settlement Accounts API](/api-payment#payment/settlement-accounts/create-account). 

Settlement accounts are available in the UK and in Euro markets and support GBP and EUR currencies.

### Creating a Settlement Account 

New settlement accounts can be created via [Console](/resources/console.md) or [API](/api-payment#payment/settlement-accounts). 

You can choose between 2 account structures: 

- __Merchant settlement accounts__ are tied to a specific merchant, which should be specified when creating the account. 
- __Acquirer settlement accounts__ can accept pay-ins from multiple merchants. When creating the account via Console, tick ‘Acquirer account’ and select “-” as the Merchant. When creating the account via API, set the `merchantId` to “-”. 

>__Note:__ For acquirer accounts, the `merchantId` must be set to “-” when calling the [get account](/api-payment#payment/settlement-accounts/get-account) and [list accounts](/api-payment#payment/settlement-accounts/list-accounts) endpoints. When calling the [get transaction](/api-payment#payment/settlement-accounts/get-transaction) and [list transactions](/api-payment#payment/settlement-accounts/list-transactions) endpoints, you can set the merchantId to “-”, which returns all transactions for the acquirer account, or a you can provide a specific `merchantId`, which limits the responses to the merchant-specific transactions.

### Setting up payout accounts 

Funds in settlement accounts should be paid out to a corporate account, called a payout account. 

You can set the payout account when creating a settlement account’s configuration, either in Console or with the Settlement Accounts API, or add one later. Due to the sensitive nature of payouts, payout accounts can only be configured once per settlement account and can’t be updated without [contacting support](https://support.tink.com). 

### Paying into settlement accounts 

Payments made to a settlement account are called pay-ins. Pay-ins come in three types: 

| Type | Description |
| -- | -- |
| `PAYIN` | A successfully reconciled payment made into a settlement account using Tink Payments |
| `MERCHANT_PAYIN` | Any payment made from your pre-configured `payoutAccount` |
| `EXTERNAL_PAYIN` | Any pay-in that Tink can't reconcile |

### Pay-ins with Tink APIs 

To pay into a settlement account using Auto Payments, create an Auto Payment mandate using the `https://api.tink.com/payments/v1/mandates` endpoint.   

A few things to keep in mind when creating the mandate: 
1. Set the `payeeAccountType` to `SETTLEMENT_ACCOUNT` 
2. Set the `payeeAccountNumber` to the UUID of the Settlement Account 
3. The `merchant_id` must be included in the mandate creation request  

__Example create mandate request__
```json
{
  "sdkParams": { 
    "locale": "en_GB", 
    "market": "GB", 
    "redirectUri": "https://localhost:3000/callback", 
    "appUri": "example://open" 
  }, 
  "mandate": { 
    "type": "AUTO_PAYMENT", 
    "scheme": "VISA_A2A", 
    "merchantId": "75747b62-d2fe-4d78-866e-c01eab988f0a", 
    "parameters": { 
      "maximumIndividualAmount": { 
        "valueInMinorUnit": 500, 
        "currencyCode": "GBP" 
      }, 
      "periodicLimits": [ 
        { 
          "type": "DAY", 
          "alignment": "MANDATE", 
          "amount": { 
            "type": "MAXIMUM", 
            "valueInMinorUnit": 500, 
            "currencyCode": "GBP" 
          } 
        } 
      ], 
      "startDate": "2025-01-12T00:00:00Z", 
      "endDate": "2026-01-12T00:00:00Z" 
    }, 
    "payer": { 
      "financialInstitutionId": "01234567-1234-1234-1234-123456789123", 
      "account": { 
        "type": "SORT_CODE", 
        "number": "1234513244343", 
        "holder": { 
          "firstName": "John", 
          "lastName": "Doe" 
        } 
      }, 
      "user": { 
        "id": null, 
        "externalId": "12345", 
      } 
    }, 
    "payee": { 
      "account": { 
        "type": "SETTLEMENT_ACCOUNT", 
        "number": "530ad3ea-fb5d-44c6-92d3-c3e9a53073b3", 
        "holder": { 
          "businessName": "Acme Inc." 
        } 
      } 
    }, 
    "riskData": { 
      "paymentContextCode": "BILLING_GOODS_AND_SERVICES_IN_ADVANCE", 
      "paymentPurposeCode": "UBIL" 
    }
  }
}  
```

__Example response__
```json
{ 
  "id": "7c4d684e-601b-4880-973d-1d5405f6d6bd", 
  "links": { 
    "tinkLinkUri": "https://link.tink.com/1.0/mandate/flow?flow_id=7c4d684e-601b-4880-973d-1d5405f6d6bd" 
  }, 
  "createdTime": "2025-05-01T00:00:00Z", 
  "status": "PROCESSING", 
   "artefacts": [ 
    { 
      "type": "MANDATE",

    },

      "type": "USER", 
      "id": "6e68cc6287704273984567b3300c5823" 
    } 
  ] 
}
```

Once you’ve created a mandate, allow the end user to authenticate the Auto Payment mandate by redirecting them to the Tink Link URI that you received in response. 

Once the mandate has been authenticated, initiate an Auto Payment to the settlement account by using the `https://api.tink.com/payment/v2/mandate-payments` endpoint. Use the `mandateId` that was issued when creating the Auto Payment mandate.

>__Note:__ The `remittanceInformation.value` can be up to 10 characters. Tink will add an 8-character prefix to the reference for reconciliation purposes. The complete reference string is returned in the response to the Mandate payment request.

For more information on how to create a mandate and initiate an Auto Payment, see Initiate your first Auto Payment.

```json
{ 
  "mandateId": "c63dc11e-b210-4a96-9461-2061389789e7",

  }

```

```json
  "updatedTime": "2025-01-01T09:35:39.000Z", 
  "type": "AUTO_PAYMENT", 
  "scheme": "VISA_A2A", 
  "payee": { 
    "account": { 
      "type": "SETTLEMENT_ACCOUNT", 
      "number": "744cf927-29cd-475e-9ef2-2b11951d3cc9", 
      "holder": { 
        "businessName": "Acme Inc." 
      } 
    } 
  }, 
  "payer": { 
    "financialInstitutionId": "01234567-1234-1234-1234-123456789123", 
    "account": { 
      "type": "SORT_CODE", 
      "number": "12345613244343", 
      "holder": { 
        "firstName": "John", 
        "lastName": "Doe" 
      } 
    } 
  }, 
  "mandateId": "c63dc11e-b210-4a96-9461-2061389789e7", 
  "amount": { 
    "valueInMinorUnit": 100000, 
    "currencyCode": "GBP" 
  }, 
  "remittanceInformation": { 
    "type": "REFERENCE", 
    "value": "9vDfzcIA1234567891" 
  }, 
  "riskData": { 
    "userInteraction": "OFF_SESSION" 
  }

```

### Pay-ins with a manual transfer 

To pay in to a settlement account using a manual bank transfer, use the account identifier found in Console or returned by the [get account](/api#payment/settlement-accounts/get-account) endpoint. Typically, you make manual transfers from your `payoutAccount` to top up a settlement account so that you have enough funds to make refunds or withdrawals. 

Make sure that the transfer is made using a payment scheme and currency supported by the settlement account.

### Pay-ins with a manual transfer 

To pay in to a settlement account using a manual bank transfer, use the account identifier found in Console or returned by the [Get account](/api#payment/settlement-accounts/get-account) endpoint. Typically, you make manual transfers from your `payoutAccount` to top up a settlement account so that you have enough funds to make refunds or withdrawals.  

> Make sure that the transfer is made using a payment scheme and currency supported by the settlement account. 

## Payouts 

Payouts are payments from your settlement accounts to a user's bank account or a configured `payoutAccount`. Payouts can be one of four types: `SWEEP`, `REFUND`, `WITHDRAWAL`, and `TRANSFER`.

| Payout Type | Description |
| -- | -- |
| `SWEEP` | A transfer of a settlement account's available balance to a payout account on a scheduled basis |
| `REFUND` | A transfer of a full or partial previous transaction amount to an end-user |
| `WITHDRAWAL` | A transfer to an end-user |
| `TRANSFER` | A transfer not initiated using Tink |

> When making refunds and withdrawals, you need to include [Idempotency-Key](/api#introduction/idempotency-and-caching) in the request header. This allows users to safely retry failed operations without the risk of transferring more funds than intended. 

By default, Tink executes all payouts with SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) for EUR payments and falls back to SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) if the receiving account doesn't support inbound SCT Inst. For the UK, we use Faster Payments. If the payout is over the SCT Inst (€100,000) or Faster Payments (£1,000,000) scheme limit it will be initiated via SCT or CHAPS respectively. 

SCT Inst and Faster Payments typically settle within a few seconds, while SCT and CHAPS can take up to one business day.

### Sweeps 

A `SWEEP` is a transfer of a settlement account's available balance to a payout account according to a set schedule. When configuring a payout account, you can set the payout frequency to `DAILY`, `WEEKLY`, or `MONTHLY`. 

We initiate sweeps at 6:30AM UTC and include all pay-ins made since 6:30AM UTC at the start of the previous payout interval (daily, weekly, or monthly). How fast the `SWEEP` settles depends on the scheme used to execute the payment. 

To have enough funds after a sweep, you can either top-up through a `MERCHANT_PAYIN` or until enough regular `PAYIN` transactions have funded the account. 

Optionally, you can configure the reserved amount to set a float on the account to be held and not paid out through a `SWEEP`. This limits the number of manual top-ups you would need to otherwise do to cover eventual refunds and withdrawals.

### Refunds 

You can make a full or partial refund to an end user bank account through our [refund endpoint](/api#payment/settlement-accounts/create-refund). The refunded amount can be any amount up to the full value of the original payment. 

To initiate a refund: 
- Get the `id` of the `PAYIN` transaction to be refunded. Refunds can only be initiated from and to the same accounts. 
- Create a refund request using the `id` as the `transactionId` value. Tink will check that the transaction is eligible for a refund and that the refund `amount` doesn’t exceed the original transaction amount. 
- Tink executes the refund and updates the balance on your account. 
- Get notified of the status of the refund by either polling the [refund endpoint](/api#payment/settlement-accounts/get-refund) or by [webhook](/resources/payments/one-time-payments/set-up-settlement-accounts-one-time-payments#event-settlement-payout-updated.md). 

__Example refund request__
```json
{ 
  "amount": { 
    "currencyCode": "GBP", 
    "value": { 
      "scale": "2", 
      "unscaledValue": "5000" 
    } 
  }, 
  "metadata": { 
    "key1": "value1", 
    "key2": "value2" 
  }, 
  "reference": "Refund7ad0feabb4ab", 
  "scheme": "FASTER_PAYMENTS", 
  "transactionId": "7ad0feab-bd55-449d-aa7e-b3d3b9c62550" 
} 
```

__Example response__
```json
{ 
  "accountId": "161ec210-721f-4df5-b21c-f78a9d4c1545", 
  "amount": { 
    "currencyCode": "GBP", 
    "value": { 
      "scale": "2", 
      "unscaledValue": "5000" 
    } 
  }, 
  "createdTime": "2022-07-14T14:01:53Z", 
  "id": "b58d313a-b778-4639-8e31-c9ffc35e2d01", 
  "merchantId": "e06e47f1-8c88-47ee-9415-a4cde72ae598", 
  "metadata": { 
    "key1": "value1", 
    "key2": "value2" 
  }, 
  "reference": "Refund7ad0feabb4ab", 
  "scheme": "FASTER_PAYMENTS", 
  "status": "COMPLETED", 
  "transactionId": "7ad0feab-bd55-449d-aa7e-b3d3b9c62550", 
  "updatedTime": "2022-07-14T14:08:53Z" 
}
```

If the user’s account associated with the original transaction is no longer available, you’ll need to: 
- Instruct the user to perform a penny-drop pay-in (a pay-in for the lowest possible amount) from their new account
- Execute a withdrawal to the user for the refund amount plus the penny-drop amount. You need to execute a withdrawal and not a refund, because the amount you are sending exceeds the penny-dop transaction amount. From the user’s perspective, this is just a refund. 

Before initiating a refund, make sure that your account has sufficient funds or the refund will fail.

### Withdrawals 

Use the [Create withdrawal endpoint](/api#payment/settlement-accounts/create-withdrawal) to initiate a payout to an end-user. Withdrawals can be of any amount and can only be initiated to users that have made a pay-in to your account. Withdrawals differ from refunds in that payouts to the user can exceed the original transaction amount, while refunds cannot. 

> Make sure to grab the `id` of the most recent `PAYIN` transaction for the user when initiating the `WITHDRAWAL`. This helps ensure that the user’s account details are up to date and thus the payment is more likely to succeed.  

Before initiating a withdrawal, make sure that your account has sufficient funds or the withdrawal will fail.

## Reconciliation 

Tink matches Tink Auto Payments against the `PAYIN` transactions using the payment `reference`. If this matching fails, then transaction will be marked as an `EXTERNAL_PAYIN`. For example, this can occur if the amount is different, or the receiving bank modifies the reference in some way. 

This is done through a unique 8-character `reference` that Tink generates when creating a payment request (pay-in). When you supply the value of the `reference` (a string of up to 10 characters), Tink will append it to the reference it generated and return the complete reference string in the response.  

Notification and reporting are served back to the merchant via API, webhook and our console.

## Checking statuses 

Payment statuses give you details on the state of a payment during the payment journey. When a payment has landed on the settlement account, you receive a new payment status transition event named `SETTLED`. 

Status and transaction details can be received through: 
- [List transactions](/api#payment/settlement-accounts/list-transactions): Get a list of transactions, including payloads, made to and from the account during the designated period. 
- [Get refunds](/api-payment#payment/settlement-accounts/get-refund) or [List refunds](/api-payment#payment/settlement-accounts/list-refunds): Retrieve a specific refund or list of refunds for a specific settlement account and merchant.
- [Get withdrawals](/api-payment#payment/settlement-accounts/get-withdrawal) or [List withdrawals](/api-payment#payment/settlement-accounts/list-withdrawals): Retrieve a specific withdrawal or list of withdrawals, for a specific settlement account and merchant. 

With Settlement Accounts, you get all the statuses that you get with Auto Payments plus the status `SETTLED` for payments that have been successfully deposited into your settlement account. You also get additional statuses for payouts.

__Payout statuses__
| Status | Description |
| -- | -- |
| `PENDING` | The payout is in progress and waiting to be completed. |
| `FAILED` | The payout failed due to an error. For example, because of insufficient funds in the settlement account. |
| `COMPLETED` | The payout has been sent successfully, and money has been debited from your settlement account. |

### Webhooks 

We have webhook events available for pay-ins, payouts and status changes on the account. We recommend subscribing to the following events: 
- `settlement-transaction:created` to be notified when a transaction has occurred on your account, including both pay-ins and payouts. 
- `settlement-payout:updated` for changes to payout statuses. 
- `settlement-account:updated` for changes to account status. 

For details on how to subscribe to webhooks, see [Set up a webhook](/resources/payments/one-time-payments-notifications-and-webhooks#set-up-a-webhook.md).

#### Event: settlement-transaction:created 

This event is fired when a transaction that corresponds to an existing settlement account for any of the users of your app is created. 

This happens if a: 
- `PAYIN` has been processed 
- `SWEEP` has been executed 
- `REFUND` has completed 
- `WITHDRAWAL` has completed

__Event content__

| Field     | Type     | Description     | Required     |
| ---------- | ---------- | ---------- | ---------- |
| `merchant_id` | string | The merchant ID for which the transaction was created.  | Yes |
| `account_id` | string | The settlement account ID for which the transaction was created. | Yes |
| `transaction_id` | string | The transaction that triggered the event. | Yes |
| `amount` | unscaled_value:number, scale: number | The transaction amount. | Yes |
| `currency_code` | string | The currency of the transaction. | Yes |
| `timestamp` | Date | The timestamp for when the notification was created. | Yes |
| `reference` | string | The transaction's reference. | No |
| `account_balance` | unscaled_value:number, scale: number | The current balance of the account after the transaction has been completed. | Yes |
| `paymentRequestId` | string | The identifier of the settlement payment request. This identifier is also present in the Mandate Payment request response. | No |
| `payer_account` | identifier: string, type: string | The source account of the transaction. | Yes |
| `payee_account` | identifier: string, type: string | The destination account of the transaction. | No |
| `metadata` | Map of string, string | A key-value dictionary with custom metadata for the transaction | No |
| `payer_name` | string | The name associated with source account | No |
| `payee_name` | string | The name associated with destination account | No |
| `type` | string | The transaction type. Example values: `PAYIN`, `SWEEP`, `REFUND`, `WITHDRAWAL`, etc. | No |
| `original_transaction_id` | string | The transaction ID for which a `SWEEP`, `REFUND`, or `WITHDRAWAL` has been created. | No |
| `refund_id` | string | The ID of the refund, if the transaction type is `REFUND`. | No |

__Example settlement-transaction:created event__
```json
{
  "content": {
    "merchantId": "73f97f20-2ee4-4aa4-8512-8b40cc493895",
    "accountId": "530ad3ea-fb5d-44c6-92d3-c3e9a53073b3",
    "transactionId": "31514ed1-fef4-46f0-a45b-7fba0f751e7a",
    "amount": 23.0,
    "currencyCode": "GBP",
    "timestamp": 1685091120000,
    "reference": "YbudeDP7xzs",
    "accountBalance": 23.00,
    "paymentRequestId": "cb3421e65c8f4de182b8bb5949460c8b",
    "payerAccount": {
      "identifier": "12345613244343",
      "type": "SORT_CODE"
    },
    "payeeAccount": {
      "identifier": "10000031510604",
      "type": "SORT_CODE"
    },
    "originalTransactionId": "",
    "type": "PAYIN",
    "refundId": "",
    "payerName": "John Doe",
    "payeeName": ""
  },
  "event": "settlement-transaction:created"
}
```

#### Event: settlement-payout:updated 

This event is fired when a payout of type `SWEEP`, `REFUND` or `WITHDRAWAL` has been executed and has reached one of the two final states: `COMPLETED` or `FAILED`.

__Example settlement-transaction:created event__
```json
{
  "content": {
    "id": "14af5bf1-5f6d-45ea-bf6e-a732a6a2325e",
    "type": "REFUND",
    "merchantId": "73f97f20-2ee4-4aa4-8512-8b40cc493895",
    "accountId": "530ad3ea-fb5d-44c6-92d3-c3e9a53073b3",
    "appId": "4d2328776f2346a2bb0e5f1289c99b71",
    "payeeName": "John Doe",
    "payeeAccount": {
      "identifier": "12345613244343",
      "type": "SORT_CODE"
    },
    "amount": 23.00,
    "currencyCode": "GBP",
    "reference": "YbudeDP7xzs",
    "metadata": {},
    "timestamp": 1685091140246,
    "status": "FAILED",
    "statusMessage": "Vendor has returned an error response."
  },
  "event": "settlement-payout:updated"
}
```

#### Event: settlement-account:updated 

This event is fired when the status of an existing settlement account is updated, meaning it has transitioned between `ENABLED`, `SUSPENDED` or `TERMINATED`.

__Event content__

| Field | Type | Description | Required |
| ---------- | ---------- | ---------- | ---------- |
| `merchant_id` | string | The merchant ID for which the transaction was created. | Yes |
| `account_id` | string | The settlement account ID for which the transaction was created. | Yes |
| `status` | string | The updated status for the corresponding settlement account. Example values: `ENABLED`,`SUSPENDED`, and `TERMINATED`. | Yes |

__Example settlement-account:updated event__
```json
{ 
  "content": {
    "merchantId": "73f97f20-2ee4-4aa4-8512-8b40cc493895",
    "accountId": "530ad3ea-fb5d-44c6-92d3-c3e9a53073b3",
    "status": "ENABLED"
  },
  "event": "settlement-account:updated"
}
```

# Test different Auto Payment scenarios 

Test your integration in a sandbox environment without using real bank credentials. 

## Prerequisites

- [Set up your Tink Console account](/resources/console/set-up-your-tink-account.md) and create a sandbox app. 

## Demo Bank

**Demo Bank** is a simulated bank that lets you to test Tink products without using real bank credentials. Even without using real bank credentials, you can still try real-world scenarios. This is done in a sandbox environment where you can test your end-user flow before it goes into production. 

Your demo credentials are found inside Console, so let's start there. 
1. [Log in to Console](https://console.tink.com/login)
2. Select **Demo Bank**
3. Select your **Product** (in this case, Payments) and your **Market**

!https://images.ctfassets.net/tmqu5vj33f7w/1gNdS9hj4IfA4iQUFQKy2Z/af52041580f242f0775207172e00856f/Demo_bank-payments.png
*Demo Bank user credentials for Payments in the United Kingdom market.*

For testing authorizing an Auto Payment mandate in Demo Bank, we'll use **User 1**.

## Select a test financial institution 

The first thing to do is to find the `financialInstitutionId` you'll use when creating an Auto Payment mandate. To learn which `financialInstitutionId` to use to test with Demo Bank, query the [providers endpoint](/api#connectivity/provider/list-providers-for-a-market). Set the `pisCapability` query parameter to `AUTO_PAYMENT` and the `includeTestProvider` query parameter to `true`, like so:

```
https://api.tink.com/api/v1/providers/GB?
pisCapability=AUTO_PAYMENT&includeTestProviders=true
```

## Initiate an Auto Payment using Demo Bank 

After you select a Demo Bank financial institution, you can create an Auto Payment mandate to generate a Tink Link URL, which allows you to authorize the mandate using Demo Bank. To do this, follow the first four steps in the [Initiate your first Auto Payment](/resources/payments/variable-recurring-payments/initiate-your-first-auto-payment.md) article in this order: 

- [Authenticate your client for mandate creation](/resources/payments/variable-recurring-payments/initiate-your-first-auto-payment#authenticate-your-client-for-mandate-creation.md)
- [Create a mandate](/resources/payments/variable-recurring-payments/initiate-your-first-auto-payment#create-a-mandate.md)
- [Authorize a mandate](/resources/payments/variable-recurring-payments/initiate-your-first-auto-payment#authorise-a-mandate.md)
- [Check the mandate status](/resources/payments/variable-recurring-payments/initiate-your-first-auto-payment#check-the-mandate-status.md)

> **Note:** When creating the mandate, make sure to specify the `financialInstitutionId` received in response to the request described in **Select a test financial institution**.

Once the mandate has been authorized, you can initiate an Auto Payment using the mandate. To do this, follow step five, six and seven in the Initiate your first Auto Payment article: 

- [Authenticate your client for payment initiation](/resources/payments/variable-recurring-payments/initiate-your-first-auto-payment#authenticate-your-client-for-auto-payment-creation.md)
- [Initiate a payment](/resources/payments/variable-recurring-payments/initiate-your-first-auto-payment#initiate-a-payment.md)
- [Check the payment status](/resources/payments/variable-recurring-payments/initiate-your-first-auto-payment#initiate-a-payment.md)

# Initiate your first Auto Payment

Source: https://docs.tink.com/resources/auto-payments/initiate-your-first-auto-payment.md

# Initiate your first Auto Payment 

Learn how to create an Auto Payment mandate and initiate your first Auto Payment. 

## Prerequisites

- Set up your Tink Console account, create a sandbox app and get your API credentials. 
- Make sure that the following client scopes are enabled for your app: `user:create`, `mandates`, `user:read`, `mandate-payments`, `mandates:readonly` 
- Make sure that Auto Payments is enabled for your app. If you aren't sure whether it's enabled or not, contact [Tink Support](/resources/support/how-to-find-technical-support.md).


The steps to initiate your first Auto Payment must be followed in order: 

1. Authenticate your client for mandate creation  
2. Create a mandate  
3. Authorize a mandate 
4. Check the mandate status  
5. Authenticate your client for payment initiation  
6. Initiate a payment 
7. Check the payment status  
8. Revoke a mandate  

## 1. Authenticate your client for mandate creation 

To create an Auto Payment mandate, you need to generate a client access token with the scopes: `user:create`, `mandates`, `user:read`, `mandates:readonly` 

For more information on how to get an access token, see  [Get access token](/api#general/oauth/get-access-token) in the API reference. 

>**Note:** access tokens expire and must be renewed, typically after 30 minutes. 

**Example authentication request**
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.tink.com/api/v1/oauth/token \
-H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
-H 'Accept: application/json' \
-d 'client_id={YOUR_CLIENT_ID}' \
-d 'client_secret={YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET}' \
-d 'grant_type=client_credentials' \ 
-d 'scope=user:create,mandates,user:read'
```

**Example response**
```json
{ 
    "token_type": "bearer", 
    "expires_in": 1799, 
    "access_token": "{YOUR_CLIENT_ACCESS_TOKEN}", 
    "scope": "user:create,mandates,user:read", 
    "id_hint": null 
}
```

## 2. Create a mandate 

To create an Auto Payment mandate, use the `https://api.tink.com/payments/v1/mandates` endpoint. When calling this endpoint, Tink issues a response that includes a `flowId` together with a Tink Link URI, as well as a `mandateId` and `userId`. 

Keep a few things in mind when creating the mandate: 
- If a `startDate` is not specified, then the mandate is valid from the mandate authorization date. 
- If an `endDate` is specified, then the end user needs to go through an authentication journey before or on that date. 
- The period alignment of periodic limits is always `MANDATE`, which means that a period starts on the `startDate` or the date when the mandate was authorized. 
- If a `financialInstitutionId` is not specified, the end user will be asked to select their bank in the Tink flow. 
- If a `payerAccount` is not specified, the end user will be asked to select an account at their bank. To use payer account preselection, you’ll need to first request access by contacting Sales. 
- The `redirectUri` specified must be configured for the app in Tink Console. 
- The `paymentContextCode` and `paymentPurposeCode` must match one of the codes provided during onboarding. 
- The `payeeAccount` must match one of the payee accounts provided during onboarding. 
- Mandate details can’t be updated after the mandate has been created. To change any of the parameters, revoke the existing mandate, create a new mandate, and send the end user through an authorization journey. 

For more information on how to create a mandate, see Create mandate in the API reference. 

**Example create mandate request**
```json
{
  "sdkParams": {
    "locale": "en_GB",
    "market": "GB",
    "redirectUri": "https://localhost:3000/callback",
    "appUri": "example://open"
  },
  "mandate": {
    "type": "AUTO_PAYMENT",
    "scheme": "VISA_A2A",
    "merchantId": "75747b62-d2fe-4d78-866e-c01eab988f0a",
    "parameters": {
      "maximumIndividualAmount": {
        "valueInMinorUnit": 500,
        "currencyCode": "GBP"
      },
      "periodicLimits": [
        {
          "type": "DAY",
          "alignment": "MANDATE",
          "amount": {
            "type": "MAXIMUM",
            "valueInMinorUnit": 500,
            "currencyCode": "GBP"
          }
        }
      ],
      "startDate": "2025-01-12T00:00:00Z",
      "endDate": "2026-01-12T00:00:00Z"
    },
    "payer": {
      "financialInstitutionId": "01234567-1234-1234-1234-123456789123",
      "account": {
        "type": "SORT_CODE",
        "number": "1234513244343",
        "holder": {
          "firstName": "John",
          "lastName": "Doe"
        }
      },
      "user": {
        "id": null,
        "externalId": "12345",
      }
    },
    "payee": {
      "account": {
        "type": "SORT_CODE",
        "number": "10000031510604",
        "holder": {
          "businessName": "Acme Inc."
        }
      }
    },
    "riskData": {
      "paymentContextCode": "BILLING_GOODS_AND_SERVICES_IN_ADVANCE",
      "paymentPurposeCode": "UBIL"
    }
  }
}
```

**Example response**
```json
{
  "id": "7c4d684e-601b-4880-973d-1d5405f6d6bd",
  "links": {
    "tinkLinkUri": "https://link.tink.com/1.0/mandate/flow?flow_id=7c4d684e-601b-4880-973d-1d5405f6d6bd"
  },
  "createdTime": "2025-05-01T00:00:00Z",
  "status": "PROCESSING",
   "artefacts": [
    {
      "type": "MANDATE",
      "id": "c800613b-3e8b-42d2-8932-7c1e8b0e49eb"
    },
    {
      "type": "USER",
      "id": "6e68cc6287704273984567b3300c5823"
    }
  ]
}
```

## 3. Authorize a mandate 

To allow the end user to authenticate with their chosen bank and select an account to make Auto Payments from, direct the user to the Tink Link URI that you received in response to your create a mandate request.  

When a user reaches the end of a flow, they're redirected to the callback URI that you've provided in the mandate creation request. The `flow_id` field is added to the URL. When redirected, the URL in your browser looks like this: 

`{YOUR_REDIRECT_URI}?flow_id=c63dc11e-b210-4a96-9461-2061389789e7`

## 4. Check the mandate status 

Use the `https://api.tink.com/payments/v1/mandates/{mandate-id}` endpoint to get the status of an Auto Payment mandate by using its `id` parameter. For more information on how to check the status of a mandate, see Get mandate in the API reference. 

**Example check the mandate status**
```json
curl -X GET https://api.tink.com/payment/v1/mandates/b6704301-8a12-46a5-a315-c3cebd9b899c \
-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
-H 'Authorization: Bearer {CLIENT_TOKEN}'
```

**Example response**

## Status transitions 

When a mandate is successfully created, its status is immediately set to `CREATED`. When the authorization of the mandate is successful, the mandate status transitions to `AUTHORIZED`. If a `startDate` was specified during mandate creation, the mandate will transition to `ACTIVE` on that date. Otherwise, it will immediately status transition from `AUHTORIZED` to `ACTIVE` after a successful authorization. If an `endDate` was specified during mandate creation, the mandate will transition to `EXPIRED` on that date. 

If the mandate authorization fails, the mandate remains in a `CREATED` state and the mandate authorization status is set to status `FAILED`. If the final status of the mandate could not be confirmed due to issues connecting to the bank, or if the bank doesn’t return a final status, then the status is set to `NON_CONFIRMABLE`. 

When you have initiated authorization of an Auto Payment mandate, poll the status every 30 seconds until status AUTHORIZED or FAILED is returned. 

The following illustration shows the state model for a mandate and a mandate authorization.

!https://images.ctfassets.net/tmqu5vj33f7w/5HLt8rtX6z30wl5l52suBh/b51fe38a98e2338a86f1913fc781d266/Auto_payment_status_transition.png
*Mandate and authorization state model*

### Mandate state definitions  

| State | Definition |
|--|--|
| `CREATED` | The mandate was created with initial values. A created mandate must go through authorization to be used to perform any other operation. |
| `AUTHORIZED` | The mandate was authorized and can be used to initiate Auto Payments when it reaches its start date.--|
| `ACTIVE` | The mandate can be used to initiate Auto Payments. |
| `EXPIRED` | The mandate has reached its expiration date and can no longer be used to initiate Auto Payments. | 
|  `REVOKED` | The mandate has been revoked and can no longer be used to initiate Auto Payments.  |

### Mandate authorization state definitions

| State | Definition |
|--|--|
| `INITIALISED` | A Tink Link authorization journey has been initiated but the user has not yet reached the bank authorization step. |
| `AUTHORIZING` | The user has started the authorization at the bank but has not completed the journey yet. |
| `AUTHORIZED` | The mandate has successfully been authorized and can be used to initiate Auto Payments when it reaches its start date. |
| `FAILED` | The mandate could not be authorized. Either there was an issue connecting to the bank, or the user didn’t successfully complete the authorization journey. 
| `PENDING` | The final status of the mandate could not be confirmed because of issues connecting to the bank, or the bank didn't return a final status. Tink will continue to check the status until it reaches a final state. |

## 5. Authenticate your client for auto payment creation 

Before you initiate an Auto Payment, you first must generate a new client access token with the `mandate-payments` scope.  

For more information on how to get an access token, see  [Get access token](/api#general/oauth/get-access-token) in the API reference. 

> **Note:** access tokens expire and must be renewed, typically after 30 minutes. 

**Example authentication request**
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.tink.com/api/v1/oauth/token \
-H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
-H 'Accept: application/json' \
-d 'client_id={YOUR_CLIENT_ID}' \
-d 'client_secret={YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET}' \
-d 'grant_type=client_credentials' \ 
-d 'scope=mandate-payments'
```

**Example response**
```json
{ 
    "token_type": "bearer", 
    "expires_in": 1799, 
    "access_token": "{YOUR_CLIENT_ACCESS_TOKEN}", 
    "scope": "mandate-payments", 
    "id_hint": null 
}
```

## 6. Initiate a payment  

To initiate an Auto Payment, use the `https://api.tink.com/payment/v2/mandate-payments` endpoint. Use the `mandateId` that was issued when creating the Auto Payment mandate, as described in Create a mandate. When calling this endpoint, Tink issues a response including the information you provided along with an `id` for the payment request. 

Keep a few things in mind: 
- The payment amount must adhere to the limitations set by the corresponding payment mandate’s control parameters. Specifically: 
- The payment amount can't exceed the mandate’s `maximumIndividualAmount`. 
- The cumulative amount of payments initiated during a given period can't exceed the mandate’s `periodicLimits`. 
- The `currencyCode` of the payment must match the currency code on the mandate. 
- The mandate must be in an `ACTIVE` state. 

Initiating an Auto Payment using a mandate doesn't require any further authorization by the end user. 

For more information on how to initiate an Auto Payment, see Create a mandate payment in the API reference. For more information on how to structure an idempotency key, see [Idempotency and caching](https://docs.tink.com/api#introduction/idempotency-and-caching).

**Example Auto Payment request**
```json
{
  "mandateId": "c63dc11e-b210-4a96-9461-2061389789e7",
  "amount": {
    "valueInMinorUnit": 1999,
    "currencyCode": "EUR"
  },
  "remittanceInformation" : {
    "type" : "REFERENCE",
    "value" : "INV-2023-001"
  },  
  "riskData" : {                                                                      
    "userInteraction" : "OFF_SESSION"
  }
}
```

**Example response**
```json
{
  "id": "b6704301-8a12-46a5-a315-c3cebd9b899c",
  "status": "CREATED",
  "createdTime": "2025-01-01T09:35:39.000Z",
  "updatedTime": "2025-01-01T09:35:39.000Z",
  "type": "AUTO_PAYMENT",
  "scheme": "VISA_A2A",
  "payee": {
    "account": {
      "type": "SORT_CODE",
      "number": "10000031510604",
      "holder": {
        "businessName": "Acme Inc."
      }
    }
  },
  "payer": {
    "financialInstitutionId": "01234567-1234-1234-1234-123456789123",
    "account": {
      "type": "SORT_CODE",
      "number": "12345613244343",
      "holder": {
        "firstName": "John",
        "lastName": "Doe"
      }
    }
  },
  "mandateId": "c63dc11e-b210-4a96-9461-2061389789e7",
  "amount": {

    "currencyCode": "GBP"
  },
  "remittanceInformation": {
```

Use the `https://api.tink.com/payments/v2/mandate payments/{mandate_payment_id}` endpoint to retrieve the status of an Auto Payment by using its `id` parameter. For more information on how to check the status of an Auto Payment, see Get mandate payment in the API reference.

### Status transitions 

When an Auto Payment request is received, its status is immediately set to `CREATED`. When the payment has been scheduled by the bank and is pending execution, the payment status transitions to `ACCEPTED`. Once the payment has been debited from the payer’s account, the payment status transition to `SETTLED_PAYER`. If the payment initiation fails, the payment status transition to `FAILED`. Check the `failureReason` to learn why. 

When you have initiated an Auto Payment, poll the status every 30 seconds until status `SETTLED_PAYER` or `FAILED `is returned. 

!https://images.ctfassets.net/tmqu5vj33f7w/69XOaT5jPOH6dq6kKOk4Bv/512fc5e28faf4926d9f33d1dd4fc36ad/Auto_payment_state_model.png
*Auto Payment state model*

| State | Definition | 
|--|--|
| `CREATED` | Payment has been created with initial values. |
| `ACCEPTED` | Payment has been scheduled by the bank and is pending execution. |
|`SETTLED_PAYER` | Payment has been debited from the payer’s account, meaning funds have left the account. Payments can still fail due to fraud checks by the bank. |
| `FAILED` | Payment was unsuccessful. For more information about the failure, see the failure reason. |

## 8. Revoke a mandate  

If an end user wants to revoke their mandate to prevent any future payments from being initiated, call the `https://api.tink.com/payment/v1/mandates/{mandate-id}:revoke` endpoint. For more information on how to revoke a mandate, see Revoke a mandate in the API reference. 

When mandate is revoked, its status transitions to `REVOKED`. If the revocation fails, the mandate remains in an `ACTIVE` state. To learn more about the state model and how to check the status of a mandate, see Check the mandate status. 

Note: A revoked it can't be reauthorized. Instead, you create new mandate and send the end user through a new authorization journey. 

**Example mandate revocation request**
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.tink.com/payment/v1/mandates/c63dc11e-b210-4a96-9461-2061389789e7:revoke \
-H 'Authorization: Bearer {CLIENT_TOKEN}' \
-H 'Idempotency-Key: b6704301-8a12-46a5-a315-c3cebd9b899c'
```

**Example response**
```json
202 Accepted
```

# Integrate Auto Payments in Android apps

Source: https://docs.tink.com/resources/auto-payments/integrate-auto-payments-in-android-apps.md

# Integrate Auto Payments in Android apps

Seamlessly launch and run the Tink SDK in your Android app environment

## Prerequisites

* You've familiarized yourself with [Console](/resources/console.md)
* You've learned how to [create a mandate](/resources/payments/variable-recurring-payments/initiate-your-auto-payment.md)


Give your users a best-in-class user experience directly in your Android app with this straightforward, lightweight integration. This is the quickest and easiest way to launch the Tink SDK from your Android app.

You can integrate the Tink SDK in your Android app with just a few steps:
- [Set up Android App Links](#set-up-android-app-links)
- [Create a mandate](#create-a-mandate)
- [Open the URL in a preconfigured WebView](#open-the-url-in-a-preconfigured-webview)
- [Handle the response](#handle-the-response-from-the-sdk)

## Set up Android App Links
Start by registering Android [App Links or deep links](https://developer.android.com/training/app-links) in your `AndroidManifest.xml`. We'll be using deep links in our examples.

To launch the SDK, you need to include two different Android App Links or deep links in your mandate creation request:
- `app_uri`, which returns the user to your app to resume the SDK flow (Ex: `example://open`).
- `redirect_uri`, which delivers the success or error response from the SDK after the flow is complete (Ex: `example://callback`)

### Example deep links
```xml

<intent-filter> 
    <action android:name="android.intent.action.VIEW" /> 
    <category android:name="android.intent.category.DEFAULT" /> 
    <category android:name="android.intent.category.BROWSABLE" /> 
     
    <data 
        android:host="open" 
        android:scheme="example" /> 
</intent-filter> 


<intent-filter>
    <action android:name="android.intent.action.VIEW" />
    <category android:name="android.intent.category.DEFAULT" />
    <category android:name="android.intent.category.BROWSABLE" />
    
    <data
        android:host="callback"
        android:scheme="example" />
</intent-filter>


<queries>
    <intent>
        <action android:name="android.support.customtabs.action.CustomTabsService" />
    </intent>
</queries>
```

## Create a mandate
[Create a mandate request](/resources/payments/variable-recurring-payments/initiate-your-first-auto-payment#create-a-mandate.md) to generate a Tink Link URI which is used to launch the SDK. Provide the required parameters as well as the app_uri you defined previously. 

### Example URL
```
https://link.tink.com/1.0/payment-mandate/vrp
  ?flow_id=7272b843-54bf-49e9-9c21-a733bb533e4d&locale=en_GB
  &market=GB
  &client_id=446b59139cd84885aa85e74b6e836377
  &redirect_uri=https://localhost:3000/callback&app_uri=example://open
```

>__NOTE__: The `app_uri` and `redirect_uri` must be valid URIs, such as App Links or a custom URL scheme including a host fragment.  For example, `example://open` works, but `example://` would not.

## Open the URL in a preconfigured WebView
Open your URL in a `WebView` and add the following `WebViewClient` implementation. This keeps the SDK navigation within the web view, opens app redirects using the intent handler and opens web redirects in a browser activity. Web redirects can't be opened directly in the `WebView` because they're blocked by certain banks.

### Example WebViewClient implementation
```kotlin
val webView = findViewById<WebView>(R.id.web_view)
webView.settings.javaScriptEnabled = true
webView.settings.domStorageEnabled = true
webView.webViewClient = object : WebViewClient() {
    override fun shouldOverrideUrlLoading(view: WebView?, url: String?): Boolean {
        val context = view!!.context
        val uri = Uri.parse(url)
        if (uri.host == "link.tink.com") { // Handle link.tink.com navigation in the web view
            return false
        } else { // Open external navigation using the system handler
            if (CustomTabsClient.getPackageName(context, null) != null) { // Open in custom tab if available
                val customTabsIntent = CustomTabsIntent.Builder().build()
                customTabsIntent.intent.addFlags(Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_EXCLUDE_FROM_RECENTS)
                customTabsIntent.intent.addFlags(Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_NO_HISTORY)
                customTabsIntent.intent.addFlags(Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK)
                customTabsIntent.launchUrl(context, uri)
                return true
            } else { // Open in system browser
                val intent = Intent(Intent.ACTION_VIEW, uri)
                .addFlags(Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK)
                context.startActivity(intent)
                return true
            }
        }
    }
}

val url: String = ... // Your SDK URL
webView.loadUrl(url)
```

## Handle the response from the SDK
The SDK sends messages through query parameters appended to the `redirect_uri`. Capture these messages from the SDK in `onCreate` or `onNewIntent`.

### Example response handling
```kotlin
override fun onNewIntent(intent: Intent?) {
    super.onNewIntent(intent)

    intent?.data?.let { uri ->
        if (uri.host == "callback") {
            val paymentRequestId = uri.getQueryParameter("flow_id")
            ... // Use `flow_id` to retrieve information about your payment or transfer
        }
    }
}
```
### Success response parameters
Tink appends the following parameters to the `redirect_uri` after a successful SDK journey.
| Parameter | Availability | Description |
|--|--|--|
| `flow_id` | Always | The identifier of the Tink flow. |

**Example success response**
```
https://myapp.com/callback?flow_id=123
```

## Design considerations
The SDK user interface has its own navigation bar. To avoid double navigation bars, present the SDK flow as a modal, or place it in such a way that any top navigation bars in your app aren't visible.

By default, the SDK displays error screens to your users prior to delivering the error response to your app. This means you don’t need to present error details to the user yourself.

## Other integration options
While there are other ways to launch the SDK, we recommend following the implementation described in this guide. Each alternative comes with its own drawbacks.

### System Browser
Launching the SDK in the system browser worsens the user experience by taking the user out of your app environment and preventing the use of automatic redirects.

# Integrate Auto Payments in iOS apps

Source: https://docs.tink.com/resources/auto-payments/integrate-auto-payments-in-ios-apps.md

# Integrate Auto Payments in iOS apps

Seamlessly launch and run the Tink SDK in your iOS app environment

## Prerequisites

* You've familiarized yourself with [Console](/resources/console.md)
* You've learned how to [create a mandate](/resources/payments/variable-recurring-payments/initiate-your-first-auto-payment.md)

Give your users a best-in-class user experience directly in your iOS app with this straightforward, lightweight integration. This is the quickest and easiest way to launch the Tink SDK from your iOS app.

You can integrate the Tink SDK in your iOS app with just a few steps:
- [Associate a universal link or custom URL scheme with your app](#associate-a-universal-link-with-your-app)
- [Create a mandate](#create-a-mandate)
- [Open the URL in a preconfigured WKWebView](#open-the-url-in-a-preconfigured-wkwebview)
- [Handle the response](#handle-the-response-from-the-sdk)

## Associate a universal link with your app
Start by associating a [universal link](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode/supporting-universal-links-in-your-app) or [custom URL scheme](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode/defining-a-custom-url-scheme-for-your-app) with your app. We recommend using universal links to avoid the “Open this page in YourAppName“ prompt in Mobile Safari during redirects, and this is what we'll use in our examples.

To launch the SDK, you need to include two different universal links or deep links in your mandate creation request:
- `app_uri`, which returns the user to your app and resumes the SDK flow (Ex: `https://myapp.com/open`).
- `redirect_uri`, which delivers the success or error response from the SDK after the flow is complete (Ex: `https://myapp.com/callback`)

>__NOTE__: The `app_uri` and `redirect_uri` must be valid URIs, such as universal links or a custom URL scheme including a host fragment.  For example, `example://open` works, but `example://` would not.

## Create a mandate
[Create a mandate request](/resources/payments/variable-recurring-payments/initiate-your-first-auto-payment#create-a-mandate.md) to generate a Tink Link URI which is used to launch the SDK. Provide the required parameters as well as the `app_uri` you defined previously. 

### Example URL
```
https://link.tink.com/1.0/payment-mandate/vrp
  ?flow_id=7272b843-54bf-49e9-9c21-a733bb533e4d
  &locale=en_GB&market=GB
  &client_id=446b59139cd84885aa85e74b6e836377
  &redirect_uri=https://localhost:3000/callback
  &app_uri=example://open 
```

## Open the URL in a preconfigured WKWebView
Open your URL in a `WKWebView` and add the following implementation. This keeps the SDK navigation within the web view, opens app redirects using the system handler and opens web redirects in an in-app browser. Web redirects can't be opened directly in the `WKWebView` because they're blocked by certain banks.

```swift
import UIKit
import WebKit
import SafariServices

extension Notification.Name {
    static let linkCallback = Notification.Name("Link.Callback")
    static let linkOpen = Notification.Name("Link.Open")
}

final class LinkViewController: UIViewController { 
    let url: URL 

    private let webView = WKWebView() 
    private var safariViewController: SFSafariViewController? 

    init(url: URL) { 
        self.url = url 
        super.init(nibName: nil, bundle: nil) 
    } 

    required init?(coder aDecoder: NSCoder) { 
        fatalError("init(coder:) has not been implemented") 
    } 

    override func viewDidLoad() { 
        super.viewDidLoad() 

        webView.navigationDelegate = self 
        webView.translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false 
        view.addSubview(webView) 

        NSLayoutConstraint.activate([ 
            webView.topAnchor.constraint(equalTo: view.topAnchor), 
            webView.leadingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: view.leadingAnchor), 
            webView.trailingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: view.trailingAnchor), 
            webView.bottomAnchor.constraint(equalTo: view.bottomAnchor), 
        ]) 
        webView.load(URLRequest(url: url)) 

        NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(forName: .linkOpen, object: nil, queue: .main) { [weak self] notification in 
            self?.safariViewController?.dismiss(animated: true) 
            self?.safariViewController = nil 
        } 

        NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(forName: .linkCallback, object: nil, queue: .main) { [weak self] notification in 
            guard let url = notification.userInfo?["url"] as? URL else { return } 
            let components = URLComponents(url: url, resolvingAgainstBaseURL: true) 
            if let paymentRequestId = components?.queryItems?.first(where: { $0.name == "flow_id" })?.value { 
                // Successful response: Use `flow_id` to retrieve information about your payment or transfer
            } else if let error = components?.queryItems?.first(where: { $0.name == "error" })?.value, error != "USER_CANCELLED" { 
                // Error response: Handle `error` code 
            }           
            self?.dismiss(animated: true) 
        } 
    } 
} 

extension LinkViewController: WKNavigationDelegate { 
    func webView(_ webView: WKWebView, decidePolicyFor navigationAction: WKNavigationAction, decisionHandler: @escaping (WKNavigationActionPolicy) -> Void) { 
        if let url = navigationAction.request.url { 
            if url.host == "link.tink.com", navigationAction.targetFrame != nil { 
                // Handle same page link.tink.com navigation in the web view 
                decisionHandler(.allow) 
            } else if ["http", "https"].contains(url.scheme) { 
                // Attempt to open HTTP(s) navigation using universal links, otherwise present in embedded in-app browser 
                UIApplication.shared.open(url, options: [.universalLinksOnly: true], completionHandler: { [weak self] success in 
                    guard !success else { 
                        return 
                    } 
                    let safariViewController = SFSafariViewController(url: url) 
                    safariViewController.modalPresentationStyle = .formSheet 
                    self?.present(safariViewController, animated: true) 
                    self?.safariViewController = safariViewController 
                }) 
                decisionHandler(.cancel) 
            } else { 
                // Open custom scheme deep links (eg. bankid://) using the system handler 
                UIApplication.shared.open(url, options: [:], completionHandler: nil) 
                decisionHandler(.cancel) 
            } 
        } else { 
            decisionHandler(.allow) 
        } 
    } 
} 

extension AppDelegate {
    func application(_ app: UIApplication, open url: URL, options: [UIApplication.OpenURLOptionsKey : Any] = [:]) -> Bool {
        if url.host() == "open" {
            NotificationCenter.default.post(name: .linkOpen, object: nil, userInfo: ["url": url])
            return true
        }

        if url.host() == "callback" {
            NotificationCenter.default.post(name: .linkCallback, object: nil, userInfo: ["url": url])
            return true
        }

        return false
    }
}

extension SceneDelegate {
    func scene(_ scene: UIScene, openURLContexts URLContexts: Set<UIOpenURLContext>) {
        guard let url = URLContexts.first?.url else { return }

        if url.host() == "open" {
            NotificationCenter.default.post(name: .linkOpen, object: nil, userInfo: ["url": url])
        }

        if url.host() == "callback" {
            NotificationCenter.default.post(name: .linkCallback, object: nil, userInfo: ["url": url])
        }
    }
}
```

## Handle the response from the SDK
The SDK will return the result of the operation as query parameters appended to the `redirect_uri`. You can access the `payment_request_id` in the `Notification.Name.linkCallback` notification observer as demonstrated in the [preconfigured WKWebView example](#open-the-url-in-a-preconfigured-wkwebview).

### Success response parameters
Tink appends the following parameters to the redirect_uri after a successful SDK journey.

| Parameter | Availability | Description |
|--|--|--|
| `flow_id` | Always | The identifier of the Tink flow. |

**Example success response**
```
https://myapp.com/callback?flow_id=123
```

## Design considerations
The SDK user interface has its own navigation bar. To avoid double navigation bars, present the SDK flow as a modal. If this isn't possible, avoid placing it in any `UINavigationController` or `NavigationStack` that has a visible navigation bar.

By default, the SDK displays error screens to your users prior to delivering the error response to your app. This means you don’t need to present  error details to the user yourself.

## Other integration options
While there are other ways to launch the SDK, we recommend following the implementation described in this guide. Each alternative comes with its own drawbacks.

### UIWebView
`UIWebView` is deprecated as of iOS 12.0. Use `WKWebView` instead to get the same behavior.

### SFSafariViewController
`SFSafariViewController` is incompatible with the SDK URL's `app_uri`.

### System Browser
Launching the SDK in the system browser worsens the user experience by taking the user out of your app environment and preventing the use of automatic redirects.

# Handle Auto Payment errors

Source: https://docs.tink.com/resources/auto-payments/handle-auto-payment-errors.md

# Handle Auto Payment errors

Learn about the error response formats, error codes and failure reasons you may encounter during the Auto Payment API request processing. 

When integrating with the Auto Payment APIs and SDK, it is essential to understand how errors and failures are reported and handled. This guide provides a comprehensive overview of the error response formats, common error and failure scenarios, and recommended handling strategies for developers. 

This article contains three sections: 

1. __API errors__: Errors returned directly by the Auto Payment APIs, including their structure and typical causes. 
2. __Mandate authorization failures__: Reasons why a mandate authorization may fail, how these failures are communicated, failure reasons you may encounter, and best practices for responding to these scenarios. 
3. __Payment failures__: Common causes of payment processing failures, failure reasons you may encounter, and best practices for responding to these scenarios. 

> **Note:** New errors and failure reasons may be introduced over time and will be considered a non-breaking API change. To ensure robust integration, always design your error handling to gracefully handle unknown codes. 

## API errors 

Tink will return a HTTP status code 4XX or 5XX whenever there is something wrong with a request towards our platform. When an error occurs, the Auto Payment APIs (mandate and mandate payments APIs) returns a structured error response following the [RFC 7807: Problem Details for HTTP APIs](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7807 "RFC 7807: Problem Details for HTTP APIs") standard. 

### Standard error response structure 

The standard error response structure consists of the following field:  

- `type`: A URI reference identifying the problem type. This is consistent across all occurrences of the same error type. 
- `title`: A short, human-readable summary of the problem type. 
- `status`:The HTTP status code for this occurrence of the problem. 
- `detail`: A human-readable explanation specific to this occurrence of the problem. 
- `instance`: A URI reference identifying the specific occurrence of the problem. 

__Example response:__

    { 
     "type": "urn:errors:invalid-argument", 
     "title": "Invalid argument", 
     "status": 400, 
     "detail": "The request contains invalid arguments", 
     "instance": "urn:uuid:0b5c1a25-724c-44a7-9ac2-237ed6a84732", 
     "invalidParameters": [ 
      {  
       "name": "amount", 
       "reason": "Payment amount exceeds mandate's maximum individual payment amount." 
       } 
     ] 
    } 

### API error codes 

Auto Payment API errors are organised into three categories based on the problem type. 

1. Invalid request arguments  
2. Request preconditions failed 
3. Errors without a problem type 

### 1. Invalid request arguments 

- __HTTP Status Code__: 400 Bad Request  
- __Problem Type__: urn:errors:invalid-argument 

These errors occur when the request contains invalid or malformed data. The response includes an `invalidParameters` array that identifies which parameters are invalid and why. 

__Error response example:__ 

    { 
     "type": "urn:errors:invalid-argument", 
     "title": "Invalid argument", 
     "status": 400, 
     "detail": "The request contains invalid arguments", 
     "instance": "urn:uuid:8e03978e-40d5-43e8-bc93-6894a57f9324", 
     "invalidParameters": [ 
       { 
        "name": "amount", 
        "reason": "Payment amount exceeds mandate's maximum individual payment amount." 
       } 
     ] 
    } 

__Common invalid argument errors__

`POST/payment/v2/mandate-payments` 

| Parameter name     | Reason     
| ---------- | ---------- | 
| amount         | <ul><li>Payment amount exceeds mandate's maximum individual payment amount.</li><li>Payment would exceed mandate's maximum amount per period.</li><li>Amount cannot be null</li></ul>        | 
| amount.currencyCode         | <ul><li>Currency code is required</li><li>Currency must be GBP  </li></ul>          | 
| amount.valueInMinorUnit         | Amount value is required        | 
| currency         | Payment currency does not match mandate currency.        | 
| Idempotency-Key         | Multiple idempotency key headers found. Only one idempotency key is allowed per request.        | 
| mandateId        | <ul><li>Mandate id cannot be null</li><li>Mandate id is in invalid format. Must be UUID v4.  </li></ul>               | 
| participantId        | Participant not found. The merchant/organization is not onboarded on the specified scheme for the product type.        | 
| productType        | Participant not found. The merchant/organization is not onboarded on the specified scheme for the product type.        | 
| remittanceInformation.type         | Value must be REFERENCE       | 
| remittanceInformation.value        | <ul><li>Maximum number of characters for remittance information is 31. </li><li>The remittance information value is missing. </li><li>Maximum number of characters for remittance information is 10. (Settlement Account payments only)</li></ul>       | 
| riskData.psuInteraction        | Value must be one of: [IN_SESSION, OFF_SESSION]      | 
| schemeType        | Participant not found. The merchant/organization is not onboarded on the specified scheme for the product type.        | 
| settlementAccount.notFound         | Settlement Account not found for the provided merchant and account details.       | 

`GET /mandates/{mandateId}` 

| Parameter name     | Reason     
| ---------- | ---------- | 
| mandateId          | The mandate id is in invalid format. Must be in UUID v4. | 

`POST /mandates/{mandateId}:revoke` 

| Parameter name     | Reason     
| ---------- | ---------- | 
| mandateId          | The mandate id is in invalid format. Must be in UUID v4. | 

### 2. Request preconditions failed

- __HTTP Status Code__: 400 Bad Request  
- __Problem Type__: urn:errors:precondition-failed

These errors occur when the request is well-formed but cannot be processed due to the current state of the resource or business rule violations. The response includes a `violations` array with details about which preconditions failed. 

Error response example: 

    { 
     "type": "urn:errors:precondition-failed", 
     "title": "Precondition failed", 
     "status": 400, 
     "detail": "Mandate must be ACTIVE. Current mandate status is: EXPIRED", 
     "instance": "urn:uuid:7d92867f-29c4-45b6-b214-5dabfc8a788d", 
     "violations": [ 
       { 
        "type": "INVALID_MANDATE_STATUS", 
        "subject": "mandates/7d92867f-29c4-45b6-b214-5dabfc8a788d" 
       } 
     ] 
    } 

__Common precondition failures__

`POST /payment/v2/mandate-payments` 

| Violation Type     | Subject     | Detail     | 
| ---------- | ---------- | ---------- | 
| INVALID_MANDATE_STATUS        | mandates/{mandateId}        | Mandate must be ACTIVE. Current mandate status is: {status}.        |
| PAYMENT_NON_COMPLIANT         | N/A        | Payment is non compliant with the legal constraints.        | 
| PSU_INTERACTIONS_NOT_ALLOWED         | N/A        | Scheme participation is not allowed for the given parameters.        | 
|PSU_INTERACTIONS_NOT_AVAILABLE        | N/A        | Scheme participation is not allowed for the given parameters.        | 
| RISK_DATA_CONTEXT_CODE_NOT_ALLOWED        | N/A        | Scheme participation is not allowed for the given parameters.        | 
| RISK_DATA_PURPOSE_CODE_NOT_ALLOWED        | N/A        | Scheme participation is not allowed for the given parameters.        | 
| SCHEME_CONFIG_NOT_AVAILABLE        | N/A        | Scheme participation is not allowed for the given parameters.        | 
| SCHEME_CONFIGURATION_NOT_FOUND        | N/A        | Scheme participation is not allowed for the given parameters.        | 
| SCHEME_STATUS_NOT_VERIFIED        | N/A        | Scheme participation is not allowed for the given parameters.        |
| SETTLEMENT_ACCOUNT_NOT_ENABLED        | {settlementAccountId}        | Settlement Account payment validation failed.        | 

### 3. Errors without a problem type

These errors use generic problem types or don't include a specific problem type URI. They cover various operational issues. For more information on possible HTTP status codes and details, see API reference for mandates and mandate payments.

__Error response example:__

    { 
     "type": "about:blank", 
     "title": "Conflict", 
     "status": 409, 
     "detail": "A request with the same Idempotency-Key for the same operation is being processed.", 
     "instance": "urn:uuid:a1b2c3d4-e5f6-4789-a012-3456789abcde" 
    } 

## Mandate authorization failures  

After a mandate is successfully created (HTTP 200), it must be authorized before it can be used for payments. The mandate authorization process may fail for several reasons. To diagnose a failure, retrieve the mandate using the Get mandate endpoint and inspect the `failureReason` field.  

!https://images.ctfassets.net/tmqu5vj33f7w/1igfyrp2thALV0Q0iSWFq2/af28f314c1aed5c495ef6c3acca3ead8/Auto_payment_status_transition.png
*Mandate and authorization state model*

__Example failed mandate authorization response:__ 

    {  
    //...
    "authorization": { 
       "createdAt": "2025-01-01T09:36:39.000Z", 
       "status": "FAILED", 
       "failureReason": "USER_CANCELED” 
    ...//  
    }

### Failure reasons 

The following table outlines the possible failures that may occur during a mandate authorization flow.  

| Failure reason     | Description     | Recommendation     |
| ---------- | ---------- | ---------- |
| USER_CANCELED | The end user actively cancelled the flow, either in Tink Link or at the bank. | Offer the user to retry. |
| AUTHORIZATION_FAILED  | The end user failed to authorize the mandate due to failed SCA. <br><br> __Note:__: Tink always ensures/confirms that an ongoing authorization at the bank is cancelled.  | Offer the user to retry. If the issue persists after one retry, advise the user to contact their bank.  |
| USER_TIMEOUT        | The flow timed out due to user inactivity, either in Tink Link or at the bank. <br><br> __Note:__ Tink always ensures/confirms that an ongoing authorization at the bank is cancelled.           | Offer the user to retry.        |
| BANK_TIMEOUT        | The bank did not respond within the required timeframe.  <br><br> __Note:__ Tink verifies that the authorization at the bank has failed. If the mandate was authorized, Tink revokes it due to missing the access token.           | Offer the user to retry. If the issue persists after one retry, escalate to Tink’s support. <br><br> __Note:__ Tink continuously monitors for sudden spikes in bank timeouts. When detected, the issue is promptly escalated to the bank. If necessary, Tink temporarily disables access to the affected bank to maintain service stability and protect user experience. |         
| BANK_REJECTED        | The bank rejected the request for unspecified reasons.           | Advise the user to contact their bank for details.        |
 | BANK_UNAVAILABLE        | The bank is temporarily unavailable due to maintenance or outage.            | Advise the user to retry later. Visit [Tink’s status page](https://status.tink.com/ "Tink's status page") and subscribe for bank status updates.        |
| INTERNAL_ERROR        | Internal processing failure at Tink          | Offer the user to retry. If the issue persists after one retry, escalate to  [Tink’s support](/resources/support "Tink's support".md).          |
| UNKNOWN_ERROR        | An unknown or unmapped error occurred.         | Offer the user to retry. If the issue persists after one retry, escalate to  [Tink’s support](/resources/support "Tink's support".md).        |

## Payment failures 

A payment that is successfully created (HTTP 200) may still fail during processing. To determine the cause, retrieve the payment using the Get mandate payment endpoint and inspect the  `failureReason` field.

!https://images.ctfassets.net/tmqu5vj33f7w/viyktc6WcT20P4T4wdpco/eec3eca8a6e1cf67b976fb1a082f48f6/Auto_payment_state_model.png
*Auto Payment state model*

__Example failed payment response:__

    {  
    //... 
    "status": "FAILED", 
     "failureReason": “INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS” 
    ...//  
    } 

### Failure reasons 

The following table outlines the possible failures that may occur during payment initiation.  

| Failure reason     | Description     | Recommendation     |
| ---------- | ---------- | ---------- |
| INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS         | Payment failed due to insufficient funds            | Notify the user that their account balance is insufficient and recommend topping up. Advise them to retry once funds are available, or confirm an automatic retry at a pre-agreed time.        |
| BANK_PAYMENT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED         | Bank rejected the payment due to exceeding the bank’s payment limits          | Notify the user that they are exceeding the bank’s payment limit. Advise them to contact their bank.         |
| MANDATE_REVOKED         | Payment failed due to mandate being revoked at the bank          | Notify the user that they have revoked their mandate and offer them to set up a new mandate.        |
| BANK_REJECTED         | The bank rejected the request for unspecified reasons.           | Advise the user to contact their bank for details.        |
| BANK_UNAVAILABLE         | The bank is temporarily unavailable due to maintenance or outage.         | Advise the user to retry later or automatically retry later.  Visit [Tink’s status page](https://status.tink.com/ "Tink's status page") and subscribe for bank status updates.        |
| INTERNAL_ERROR   | Internal processing failure at Tink          | Offer the user to retry, or perform an automatic retry. If the issue persists after one retry, escalate to  [Tink’s support](/resources/support "Tink's support".md).        |
| UKNOWN_ERROR         | An unknown or unmapped error occurred.         | Offer the user to retry, or perform an automatic retry. If the issue persists after one retry, escalate to [Tink’s support](/resources/support "Tink's support".md).        |
