# Customize Tink Link

Source: https://docs.tink.com/resources/console/customize-tink-link.md

# Customize Tink Link

Customize the look and feel of the Tink Link UI to match your branding and use case.

Customizing Tink Link helps to create a more cohesive visual experience between your app and Tink, which can improve the end-user's experience and trust. Tink offers a variety of customization options to align the look and feel of the Tink experience towards your use case and branding, directly from Console. 

To start customizing, visit [Branding & theme](https://console.tink.com/app-settings/tinklink-config) from your app settings in Console.

## Themes

You can customize both `LIGHT` and `DARK` themes. If you haven't made any customizations, then your app will use the Tink default theme. The Tink default theme is available in both `LIGHT` and `DARK`, and will display either depending on the user's browser or system settings.

!https://images.ctfassets.net/tmqu5vj33f7w/1y5mYW9L53Y6yZpjCRChjl/3472311cc2bbc34fa827f25b230744fb/Dark_mode_teaser.jpg

You can bypass the user's browser or system settings and display your `LIGHT` or `DARK` theme by passing the theme value to the `theme` parameter in your Tink Link URL.

For example, this link will display a dark theme, even if the end user's system settings are set to light mode.

```bash
# Example link that forces a DARK theme
https://link.tink.com/1.0/account-check/create-report?
  client_id={CLIENT_ID}&
  redirect_uri={REDIRECT_URI}&
  market={MARKET}&
  theme=DARK
```

## Customization options

You can customize several different elements in the Tink Link UI directly from the Console: your logo, UI colors, and some additional button styling.

!https://images.ctfassets.net/tmqu5vj33f7w/4Iss6kB9yhNHYwCsmJn9bT/a3a3dab0016632c206882e7a4752eb52/Console_Customization.jpg

> __Tip:__ Console gives you live feedback on the Tink Link UI when you make changes to the UI elements. Scroll through the screens to get a comprehensive view of what your changes will look like before saving.

### Logo

Your logo must be a PNG image, 64px (height) by 400px (width). Make sure the logo is accessible against your theme’s _Page background_ color.

!https://images.ctfassets.net/tmqu5vj33f7w/Mi1FuoC7GDC3jk5FGASGZ/bdb29bc4d8247358b64ac9ea2b17c400/Logo_instruction_-_horizontal.png

!https://images.ctfassets.net/tmqu5vj33f7w/4gEHwWso4LWpa45WBx64dp/ec109f6fe9b2b94294381d4f8b5bc352/Logo_instruction_-_whitespace.png

To upload a new logo or change an existing one, open Console, go to __[YOUR APP]__ > __App settings__ > __Branding & theme__ and select __Edit branding and theme__.

### Colors
You can apply your brand color to most elements of the Tink UI from Console, with the exception of drop shadows and gradients.

> __Tip:__ Tink provides some basic color contrast validations when you adjust colors. However, to ensure that your theme is accessible, please check that the contrast between elements and the surface they're on is WCAG compliant.

#### Text colors
These are the colors of all text not in buttons.

!https://images.ctfassets.net/tmqu5vj33f7w/7vXntSCUzMcsa9y5NWYvTE/5a3c51313b253bd510ff3f2b8b08bcc8/Console_Customization_Text.jpg

| Element | Effect |
| -- | -- |
| Primary text | Headers and primary text |
| Secondary text | Other body text, like legal text |
| Error text | Error text and stroke color for error inputs |

#### Background, stroke and icon colors
These are all the various non-text colors found in the UI. Error text is listed here because the error text and stroke color for errored inputs is always the same.

!https://images.ctfassets.net/tmqu5vj33f7w/2poajyxrBO6HrT7DtqJBgK/4e0fb38a3e2811f96d9425e48a1cb5bb/Console_Customization_Backgrounds.jpg

| Element | Effect |
| -- | -- |
| Primary color | The icon color and fill color for non-text inputs, like checkboxes and radio buttons |
| Page background | The background that the rest of the UI is placed on |
| Content background | The background of the Tink UI|
| Tinted background | The alternate background used in things like loaders or interstitials | 
| Error text | Error text and stroke for error inputs |
| Stroke | The outline for containers and inputs |

#### Button colors
The colors of buttons in the active state.
!https://images.ctfassets.net/tmqu5vj33f7w/2ZYFxj4wMKBvMyxvFa0ODO/d9ba1f6ab4933c1ac91ddabd781a5c78/Console_Customization_Buttons.jpg

| Element | Effect |
| -- | -- |
| Button background | The background color of buttons |
| Button text color | Text on buttons |

### More button styling
In addition to color, you can also customize the shape, width, and text case on the button.
!https://images.ctfassets.net/tmqu5vj33f7w/5SISa4voEtI20CIj6bCQBb/26b16ad90c41681bd47c586ad626db68/Console_Customization_Buttons.jpg
| Element | Effect |
| -- | -- |
| Shape | The shape of the button: `Pill`, `Rounded`, or `Sharp` |
| Full width | The width of the button: `ON` or `OFF` |
| Uppercase letters | Toggles uppercase letters: `ON` or `OFF` |

## Custom typography
We support custom fonts from Adobe Fonts (Typekit) and Google Fonts, as well as any custom web fonts that can be hosted by Tink. Custom fonts should support the following font weights: `400` and `600`.

> __NOTE:__ Adding custom fonts is not not available directly in Console. To configure custom fonts, [contact Support](/resources/support.md).

**Examples**

```
Font family: Helvetica, Arial (fallback)
Font source: System fonts
```

```
Font family: Roboto, Helvetica (fallback)
Font source: Google Fonts
```

```
Font family: Acumin, Arial (fallback)
Font source: Adobe Fonts (Typekit)
Font identifier: xxxxxxx
```

```
Font family: MyFont, Arial (fallback)
Font source: Tink-hosted
Font URL: https://cdn.tink.se/MyFont.css
```

# Set up your Tink Console account

Source: https://docs.tink.com/resources/console/set-up-your-tink-account.md

# Set up your Tink Console account

Tink Console is where you create, configure, and manage your apps. It's also the place where you find analytics.

## Create and verify a Console account
To get started, [sign up for a Console account](https://console.tink.com/signup). When you've signed up, open the email we've sent you. Use the link in the email to verify your account and then [log in to Console](https://console.tink.com/login).

## Product availability

By default, all our products are available to test in our sandbox environment. You can access it by creating a sandbox app.

When you’re ready to create a production app, [contact sales](https://tink.com/contact-us) or reach out to your Tink contact. After you've gone through the Know Your Business process, we'll create and configure the app for you.

## What is an app?

An app is a data bucket and security concept in the Tink platform. An app allows you to gather multiple users and their data, and access the data with a set of keys. Our recommended app setup is as follows:

- __Sandbox app__: Sandbox apps allow you to perform tests by only using test credentials and test data. Create one sandbox app per product, which you can use with our [Demo Bank](/resources/console/demo-bank.md) feature.
- __Pre-production app__ (optional): Many developers like to run tests using real credentials. For example, they might use their own or a colleague's bank credentials to test their Tink integration's end-user  experience. In this case, we suggest creating a production app and giving it a name that clearly shows it's a pre-production app. This allows you to separate test and production data.
- __Production app__: Production apps only connect with live banks and allow you to store real end-user data. This is the app you should use once you’ve tried and tested your integration and are ready to go live.

## Create your first app
To get started, we encourage you to create a sandbox app to test the products you're interested in.

Your app settings are available after you've created your first app.

> __Note__: once an app is created, you can’t change its app type.

To create your first app:
1. [Log in to Console](https://console.tink.com/login).
2. Select __Create your first sandbox app__.<br>!https://images.ctfassets.net/tmqu5vj33f7w/3oLcnD2fY7JZYyQV8doQSM/02a9c6412c7e0478eeca3c5e567dd82d/Data_card.png<br>The __Create sandbox app__ modal appears.<br>!https://images.ctfassets.net/tmqu5vj33f7w/3tEX45uUoIXAd0qRSRODIP/c04b62228155b2428051c7a9cc23a2f8/Modal.png
4. Enter an __App name__. This name is only available to other Console users who are part of your organization. This name can be changed later.
5. Enter a __Display name (public)__. This name is seen by your customers as part of the Tink flow. This name __can't__ be changed later.
6. Select __Create app__.

Your app is now created and ready to configure.

## Access your API credentials
Your API credentials are used to authenticate your app with the Tink API. This is how you find your credentials.

!https://images.ctfassets.net/tmqu5vj33f7w/YywECbz6bu652RAwgTlsg/6f45d5b143be3668cdc43c15b8822ed5/set-up-your-tink-console-account-02.png

Your API credentials are found in [__your_app__] > __App settings__ > __API client__.

In this view, there are two important keys:

- `client_id`: this is the unique ID for your app. This key is public and is instantly available once you create an app.
- `client_secret`: this is a secret key for your app. This key authenticates your app with the Tink API. Handle it confidentially. You can create up to five secrets, which you can revoke at any time. Client secrets don't exist by default, so you must create them.

### Create a client secret

1. [Log in to Console](https://console.tink.com/login).
2. From the top dropdown menu, select an app.
3. Select __App settings__.
4. Select the __API client__ tab.
5. Select __Create new client secret__.
6. Enter your Console account password.
7. Select __Create__.<br><br>Your new client secret key is displayed.
8. Copy your new secret and store it in a secure location as it can't be revealed later.

# Collaborate with others

Source: https://docs.tink.com/resources/console/console-organisations-and-collaboration.md

# Collaborate with others

Learn what options are available for collaborating and sharing access to the Console.

## Create an organisation
When you first [sign up](https://console.tink.com/signup) you enter an __Organisation name__, and after successfully registering you have created your first user account for in a new organisation. Any user with the Administrator role can later change that name in the [Organisations tab](https://console.tink.com/account/organization/users) (being the first user in an organisation you are automatically assigned the Administrator role).
<img src="//images.ctfassets.net/tmqu5vj33f7w/4GJlsRgRcJjGXrJ7xgN0ts/0ea7c24f48962b4f5e8a1bdb161f48b7/Screenshot_2020-10-23_at_13.23.50.png" width="100%" />

## Inviting and removing team members
In the Organisations tab, you can invite more users to join your organisation. For each invite you’ll select a role and email address. The invited person will receive an invite email to create an account. Once accepted, this user will now be a part of your organisation. In the same section you (as Administrator) can remove team members or change their role.
<img src="//images.ctfassets.net/tmqu5vj33f7w/PRsEp303fuORbxVloQeDl/317a612c6ce2e67530ac07542998bad1/Screenshot_2020-10-28_at_12.28.19.png" width="100%" />
## Changing organisation
If you have created an account before being invited to an organisation, you do not need to create a new account, you will just have to accept the invite to join the new organisation. This means that you will now be a member of two organisations. When logged in, you can easily switch which organisation you are viewing by selecting it in the bottom left menu - where you also find the logout button.
<img src="//images.ctfassets.net/tmqu5vj33f7w/7Cl3FIPpYkg8p541lcVexW/5e8756b757d6fceb200cc56b4b06c092/Screenshot_2020-10-23_at_13.37.46.png" width="100%" />
## Security
For increased security each user can activate two-factor authentication their account. We support both common authentication apps and recovery codes. You find these settings under the [Security section](https://console.tink.com/account/profile). In the organisation tab you can view which users have activated the two-factor authentication.
<img src="//images.ctfassets.net/tmqu5vj33f7w/30jVDOlBxsOMsn3lC9kkyx/d31f4fa557367348cc3ddff4b58966e4/Screenshot_2020-10-23_at_13.40.21.png" width="100%" />
## FAQ
__Can I be a part of multiple organisations?__

- Yes you can! Once you accept an invite you’ll be part of that organisation.

__Can you change the role of a user?__

- Administrator users can change the role of other users in the organisation.

__Can I remove an organisation or my user account?__

- Yes, contact support.

__Can I remove a user with the administrator role?__

- Yes, administrator users can remove any user in the organisation - regardless of their role.

__Is there a limit on number of members in an organisation?__

- No limitation (at the time of writing)

__Will I be logged out automatically?__

- Yes, a session is valid for 3 hours.

__How long does an invite last?__

- An invite is expired after 15 days.

# Single sign-on

Source: https://docs.tink.com/resources/console/single-sign-on-via-saml.md

# Single sign-on

Follow this guide to set up single sign-on via SAML for a Console organization.

## Prerequisites

* A [Console user](/resources/console/set-up-your-tink-account.md) that is assigned to the Administrator role
* At least one identity provider (IdP) that supports SAML (Security Assertion Markup Language)
* A metadata file from your IdP

## Introduction

We allow organizations with their own IdP to use SSO (single sign-on) via SAML to log in users to Console. When SSO is enabled, users can log in to Console via your own IdP. A user that logs in with SSO doesn't need a Console user account. SSO can be enforced so that users must log in via SSO. More than one IdP can be used for SSO.

## Set up single sign-on

1. Go to [Console](https://console.tink.com) and log in.
2. Select **Organisation** > **Settings** > **Single sign-on**.
!https://images.ctfassets.net/tmqu5vj33f7w/4QTguGvsigbLXYNLptzD5G/8bd7f9c8cd49e984bbc6a43ce41d666b/settings.png
3. Select __Add SAML identity provider__.<br><br>__Note__: You can add more than one IdP. Users with the same email address from different IdPs will be treated as the same user.<br>
4. Enter a __Name__ for your SAML identity provider.<br><br>__Note__: Some IdPs require that you provide a service provider’s (SP) metadata before you are allowed to extract IdP metadata. If this is the case, upload an incomplete IdP metadata file and update it later by selecting __Update__.
!https://images.ctfassets.net/tmqu5vj33f7w/2uTWIdfjuJdFOYkUOXx9Bh/c8a1b4b34b7b7cf788969113cdefc9d0/saml-upload.png
5. Select __Upload IdP metadata__. The file must be in the XML format.
6. Select your IdP metadata file.
7. Select __Next__.<br><br>The file is now uploaded.<br><br>The Tink service provider (SP) settings dialog appears.
!https://images.ctfassets.net/tmqu5vj33f7w/69mMNt7GavUEto6fqP8HAF/52d4775fc2b5b44fade720bb0182f462/saml-uploaded.png
8. Select __Download metadata__ to download a SAML-formatted metadata file for use with your IdP.
9. Configure the SAML attribute mappings in your IdP. Some attributes are required and authentication will fail if they are not mapped according to the table.
| Name | Value | Required | Format |
| ---- | ----- | ------ | ------ |
| `email` | The user's email address | ✅ |Email address. Example: `name@domain.com` |
| `firstName` | The user's first name | ✅ | Letters, numbers, the space character and these characters: `.-/&` |
| `lastName` | The user's last name | ✅ | Letters, numbers, the space character and these characters: `.-/&` |
| `role` | The user's role | ❌ |For a full list of allowed values, see [Role map](#role-map). |

      > The attributes `firstName`, `lastName` and `role` are updated every time a user logs in if the IdP configuration has changed since the last login. If the role attribute isn't configured, the user is assigned the `viewer` role.

10. Use the `Login URL` from the __Tink service provider (SP) settings__ dialog in step 7 to log in via your newly configured SAML connection.

When the setup is completed you can always go back to **Organisation > Settings** to find the SP settings.

### Important

- Console doesn't support IdP-initiated logins. Users must use `Login URL` to authenticate with Console.
- __Default role for new users__: If you enable SSO and assign a value to the SAML mapping `role`, Console users will be assigned to that role when they log in for the first time. If you enable SSO and do not use the SAML mapping `role`, Console users will be assigned to the __Viewer__ role when they log in for the first time.
- __IdP settings always overrule Console settings__: If you enable SSO, assign a value to the SAML mapping `role` and change an existing Console user’s role in your IdP, Console will detect that change the next time the user logs in to Console and change their Console role to what is stated in the IdP.
- To see the settings for an SP, go to __Organisation__ > __[Settings](https://console.tink.com/account/organization/settings)__ and select the name of your SAML identity provider.

!https://images.ctfassets.net/tmqu5vj33f7w/010QBWZSBHzPGbABy5kRlo/010d52e4c7122cd4a599152294445b42/saml-done.png

## Enforce single sign-on
Enforce SSO by changing your __Authentication__ method to log in with SSO via SAML. Only the organization owner has permission to enforce SSO. Before doing so, make sure there are no pending user invitations and that all non-SSO users - except the owner — have been manually removed. Enforcement cannot proceed until these conditions are met.

The owner of the organisation will not be affected when enforcing SSO. The reason for this is to avoid locking out an entire organisation from Console if the SAML configuration breaks.

To enforce SSO:

1. Go to [Console](https://console.tink.com) and log in.
2. Go to __Organisation__ > __Settings__ > __Single sign-on__.
!https://images.ctfassets.net/tmqu5vj33f7w/4QTguGvsigbLXYNLptzD5G/8bd7f9c8cd49e984bbc6a43ce41d666b/settings.png
3. Select __Edit authentication__.
!https://images.ctfassets.net/tmqu5vj33f7w/4LDie8080kclqAUYtsCh5J/9a556d7aa5e40f8bbcebf97da718ee70/SSO_authentication.png
4. Select __Members must log in with SSO via SAML__.
5. Select __Save__.

## Role map
These values can be passed in the role attribute of the SAML assertion:

| Supported values | Role |
| ---- | ----- |
| `admin` | Administrator |
| `editor` | Editor |
| `viewer` | Viewer |
| `support` | Support |

## FAQ

__Can I be a part of multiple organizations?__

No, you can’t. We see SAML users as unique users per organization.

__Can I automatically be logged out?__

You will automatically be logged out. A session is valid for 3 hours.

__When I use more than one IdP, how are users handled?__

SAML users with the same email address that exist in the same Console organization are seen as a unique user.

__How do you handle users that use different authentication methods?__

A Console organization supports multiple user authentication methods by default. See [Enforce SSO](#enforce-single-sign-on) if you only want to use SSO for authentication purposes. If more than one user have the same email address but use different authentication methods, Console will consider the users to be separate.

This is why an organization owner can't use SSO: if the SAML configuration would somehow break, it could lead to an entire organization being locked out, including the owner.

__Do you sign AuthnRequest messages?__

Yes, we do. As an SP, we have set `AuthnRequestsSigned=true`, which means that we sign the `AuthRequest` messages that we send.

__Do you support IdP-initiated login?__

No, we don’t. This is for security reasons.

__Why do I get a 403 response?__

- Login via IdP initiation isn't allowed.
- Your SAML attribute mappings are incorrect. Double-check that your fields are not misspelled and that your values aren't incorrectly formatted.

__Can you please help me with this?__

Don’t hesitate to contact [Tink Support](/resources/support/how-to-find-technical-support.md) if you have any questions or problems that you want to resolve. We’re here to help.

# Demo Bank

Demo Bank is a simulated bank that allows you to test Tink products without using real bank credentials. Even though Demo Bank doesn't use real bank credentials, it lets you try real-world scenarios and see how your end-user flow works before it goes into production.

## Prerequisites

- Go to [Set up your Tink Console account](/resources/getting-started/set-up-your-account.md) and follow all steps to create a Console account, your first sandbox app, and retrieve your API credentials.


__Demo Bank__ is a simulated bank that allows you to test Tink products without using real bank credentials. Even though Demo Bank doesn't use real bank credentials, it lets you try real-world scenarios and see how your end-user flow works before it goes into production.

Your demo credentials are found inside Console, so let's start there.

1. [Log in to Console](https://console.tink.com/login).
2. Select __Demo Bank__.
3. Select a __Product__ and a __Market__.

!https://images.ctfassets.net/tmqu5vj33f7w/1VxkCsytHgSuT25RK4rtj1/fe5a68143331f208958a6e06559396f9/account_check_demo_bank.png
*Demo Bank user credentials for Account Check in the Swedish market.*

Each user represents a different test case. In Demo Bank, the __Description__ field explains a user's purpose. For example, User 1 is used to test a successful scenario that leads to you fetching an Account Check report with full information.

!https://images.ctfassets.net/tmqu5vj33f7w/7zWyL0jOzr90bt01gQyjRJ/9768e36d0f47f03c321d9d07dd09154e/Screenshot_2023-08-02_at_09.45.18.png
Clicking on __‘User 1’__ allows you to see more details about the user. This includes credentials you might need to use when authenticating (e.g. SSN in Sweden), as well as information about the accounts of that user. 

When you have selected a Demo Bank user for your test, it's time to [build your Tink Link](/resources/account-check/verify-your-first-account#build-the-url.md). Select __Copy URL__, paste it into a browser, and hit enter.

# Ingest accounts & transactions into the Tink Platform

Source: https://docs.tink.com/resources/consumer-engagement/ingest-accounts-and-transactions.md

# Ingest accounts & transactions into the Tink Platform

Ingesting your own account data and transactions is possible using [Tink’s Connector API](https://docs.tink.com/api/connector).

## Prerequisites

* Create a [developer account](/resources/getting-started/set-up-your-account.md) and retrieve your `client_id` and `client_secret`.
* If you want your data to be persisted longer than 24h, make sure you are an [enterprise](https://tink.com/pricing) customer with [permanent users](/glossary#permanent-users.md) enabled.
* Check under [App settings](https://console.tink.com) that your OAuth client is allowed to use the following scopes: `authorization:grant`, `user:create`, `accounts:read`, `accounts:write`, `transactions:read`, `transactions:write`.
* Get a [client access token](/resources/getting-started/get-access-token.md) with the scopes `authorization:grant`, `user:create`, `accounts:read`, `accounts:write`, `transactions:read` and `transactions:write`.
* Get a [user access token](/resources/getting-started/get-access-token.md) with the scopes `accounts:read`, `transactions:read` and `credentials:read`, filling in the `externalUserId` field from the [User API](https://docs.tink.com/api#general/user) (mandatory, does not work with `userId`).

These are the steps we will go through:

1. Ingest account data to an existing user
2. Review the added accounts
3. Ingest transactions to an account
4. Verify that account/transactions has been processed and enriched
5. Verify that the transaction has been added to the account

## Ingest account data to an existing user
**Documentation**: Visit the **Account service** section in the [Connector API reference](https://docs.tink.com/api/connector/).

**Purpose**: Creates accounts for a specific `externalUserId` via the connector API. When creating the user prior to doing ingestion, you must define an `externalUserId` for the user. `external_user_id` is an identifier you associate with this user, which is unique within your app. We suggest avoiding PII and recommend using a generated ID containing only `a-z`, `0-9` and `-`. This parameter is global unique for the app. 
>**Note**: that the token used for the connector API is `YOUR_CLIENT_ACCESS_TOKEN`.

```bash
#Request example
curl -v -X POST 'https://api.tink.com/connector/users/{externalUserId}/accounts' \
-H 'Authorization: Bearer {YOUR_CLIENT_ACCESS_TOKEN}' \
-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
-d '{
  "accounts": [
    {
      "availableCredit": 20000,
      "balance": 7000,
      "closed": false,
      "externalId": "AN_EXTERNAL_ACCOUNT_ID",
      "flags": [
        "MANDATE"
      ],
      "name": "YOUR_CHECKING_ACCOUNT",
      "number": "52670208126",
      "payload": {},
      "reservedAmount": 2000,
      "type": "CREDIT_CARD"
    }
  ]
}'
```
**Response**: A successful ingestion of an account returns `HTTP 204` with no additional content. To review if data is correctly added, please verify by listing the account/s (next step in this guide).

**Common errors**:
* `HTTP 401`	(Possible reasons is expired `YOUR_CLIENT_ACCESS_TOKEN`)
* `HTTP 403 - Access forbidden` (The `YOUR_CLIENT_ACCESS_TOKEN` is most likely missing a required scope)

## Review the added accounts
**Documentation**: Visit the [Account API](https://docs.tink.com/api#data-v1/account).

**Purpose**: Returns an object with a list of the authenticated user's accounts. This list can then be reviewed to verify that the ingested information is correct. 

> **Note**: To be able to list the account, a `YOUR_USER_ACCESS_TOKEN` for the specific user must be generated and authenticated. For a detailed description of how to do this, please read the [Getting started](/resources/api-setup.md) section.

```bash
#Request example
curl -X GET 'https://api.tink.com/api/v1/accounts/list' \
-H 'Authorization: Bearer {YOUR_USER_ACCESS_TOKEN}' \
-H 'Content-Type: application/json'
```

**Response**:
```json
{
  "accounts": [
    {
      "accountNumber": "52670208126",
      "availableCredit": 20000.0,
      "balance": 5000.0,
      "bankId": "AN_EXTERNAL_ACCOUNT_ID",
      "certainDate": null,
      "credentialsId": "3360e34a8d35427f8d8add08dfd33876",
      "excluded": false,
      "favored": false,
      "id": "01df3e7a43564085a164023ea4c8ece5",
      "name": "YOUR_CHECKING_ACCOUNT",
      "ownership": 1.0,
      "payload": "{\"PARTNER_PAYLOAD\":\"{}\"}",
      "type": "CREDIT_CARD",
      "userId": "85a9632e3b3942a48844491f0054fa77",
      "userModifiedExcluded": false,
      "userModifiedName": false,
      "userModifiedType": false,
      "identifiers": "[]",
      "transferDestinations": null,
      "details": null,
      "images": {
        "icon": "https://cdn.tink.se/provider-images/placeholder.png",
        "banner": null
      },
      "holderName": null,
      "closed": false,
      "flags": "[\"MANDATE\"]",
      "accountExclusion": "NONE",
      "currencyCode": "SEK",
      "currencyDenominatedBalance": {
        "unscaledValue": 50000,
        "scale": 1,
        "currencyCode": "SEK"
      },
      "refreshed": null,
      "financialInstitutionId": null
    }
  ]
}
```
**Common errors**:
* `HTTP 400 - Authorization code not valid`
* `HTTP 401 - Could not find the OAuth client` (The specified `clientId` is invalid)
* `HTTP 409 - Account already exists`

## Ingest Transactions 
**Documentation:** Visit the **Transaction service** section in the [Connector API reference](https://docs.tink.com/api/connector/).

**Purpose**: Adds transactions to an account, historical transactions or real time transactions. 
>**Note**: Maximum 2500 transactions per request.

```bash
#Request example
curl -v -X POST 'https://api.tink.com/connector/users/{externalUserId}/transactions' \
-H 'Authorization: Bearer {YOUR_CLIENT_ACCESS_TOKEN}' \
-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
-d '{
  "autoBook": false,
  "overridePending": false,
  "transactionAccounts": [
    {
      "balance": 7000,
      "externalId": "AN_EXTERNAL_ACCOUNT_ID",
      "payload": {},
      "reservedAmount": 2000,
      "transactions": [
        {
          "amount": -98,
          "date": 1455740874875,
          "description": "Riche Teatergrillen",
          "externalId": "40dc04e5353547378c84f34ffc88f853",
          "payload": {},
          "pending": false,
          "type": "CREDIT_CARD"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "type": "BATCH"
}'
```
**Response**: A successful ingested transaction returns `HTTP 204` with no content.

**Common errors**:
* `HTTP 400`	(The payload does not pass validation, or the specified account does not exist)
* `HTTP 401 - User not found`
* `HTTP 409 - Transaction already exist`

## Verify that transactions has been processed and enriched
**Documentation**: Visit the [Credentials API](https://docs.tink.com/api#connectivity/credentials).

**Purpose**: When you have inserted a bulk of `transactions` Tink will respond with a `HTTP 204` asynchronously from the processing of transaction. The response from Tink means that the request past validation and is put on queue for ingestion. That means that the accounts/transactions will not be ready to be used via the account and transaction API instantaneously. This could take up to a few seconds. To verify that the ingested data has been enriched you need to check the credential before the ingestion. The ingested transactions are available when the credential is in the state `UPDATED` and the timestamp is later then compared to before ingestion. Note that the `YOUR_USER_ACCESS_TOKEN` shall be used as bearer token. 
>**Note**: A common error is that if no transactions has been ingested, the `statusUpdated` timestamp would be null and therefore not returned in the credentials response body.

```bash
#Request example
curl -X GET 'https://api.tink.com/api/v1/credentials' \
-H 'Authorization: Bearer {YOUR_USER_ACCESS_TOKEN}' \
-H 'Content-Type: application/json'
```

**Response**:
```json
[
  {
    "providerLatency": 0,
    "id": "3360e34a8d35427f8d8add08dfd33876",
    "providerName": "se-oxford-abstract",
    "status": "UPDATED",
    "statusPayload": "Analyserat 1 konto och 1 transaktion.",
    "statusUpdated": 1581065493317,
    "type": "PASSWORD",
    "updated": 1581065493317,
    "userId": "85a9632e3b3942a48844491f0054fa77",
    "images": {
      "icon": "https://cdn.tink.se/provider-images/placeholder.png",
      "banner": null
    },
    "psd2CredentialGenerated": false,
    "dataVersion": 1,
    "fields": {},
    "sensitivePayload": {}
  }
]
```

# Get your data into Tink platform using the Connector v2

Source: https://docs.tink.com/resources/consumer-engagement/get-your-data-into-tink-platform-using-the-connector-v2.md

# Get your data into Tink platform using the Connector v2

Use Connector v2 to ingest account and transaction data directly from your financial institution, enabling you to power the Data Enrichment product. Once data is ingested and processed, you can use features like Merchant Information and Categorised Transactions together with our Finance Management packages.

## Prerequisites

1. Make sure you app is already configured to use Data Enrichment, see article [here](/resources/data-enrichment/configure-your-application-to-use-data-enrichment.md).
2. Your app must have additional scopes enabled: `accounts:write`, `transactions:write`. In Console, go to __[your_app] > App settings > API Client > All available client scopes__. If this section doesn't list these scopes, contact [Tink Support](/resources/support/how-to-find-technical-support.md) to have the scopes enabled for you.

Most Data Enrichment features require a permanent user and access to the end-user's transaction data. There are two ways to provide this data for your app:
- Aggregation, where Tink collects the data on your behalf with the end user's consent.
- Manual ingestion, where data is pushed directly to Tink using Connector v2 API.

This guide focuses on the manual ingestion method. If you are looking for information about Aggregation, [see this article](/resources/data-enrichment/get-data-into-the-tink-platform-using-aggregation.md).

## Onboard your first user and ingest account and transaction data into Tink Platform with Connector v2

Using Connector v2 API you as an issuer, financial institution or merchant can ingest your transaction and account information to get it enriched. This is useful when your financial institution already holds end-user data and you want to bring it into the Tink Platform to power products like Data Enrichment. 

This section guides you through the core steps to get started - from authentication to data submission. You will learn how to:
1. Authenticating your client
2. Create a user
3. Ingest an account
4. Batch ingesting transactions
5. Check operation status

### Step 1. Authenticating your client

Start by authorising your application to use the Connector v2 API.
This request uses your `client_id` and `client_secret` to generate a client access token with the required scopes: `user:create`, `accounts:write`, `transactions:write`.

The Client Access Token grants - in this case - access to the endpoints used for creating users, ingesting accounts and transactions. It's valid for 30 minutes.

**Example request:**
```bash
curl -v -X POST https://api.tink.com/api/v1/oauth/token \
-d 'client_id={YOUR_CLIENT_ID}' \
-d 'client_secret={YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET}' \
-d 'grant_type=client_credentials' \
-d 'scope=user:create,accounts:write,transactions:write'
```

**Example response:**
```json
{
  "access_token": "{YOUR_CLIENT_ACCESS_TOKEN}",
  "token_type": "bearer",
  "expires_in": 1800,
  "scope": "user:create,accounts:write,transactions:write"
}
```
For more information, see complete [OAuth documentation reference](/api-general#general/oauth).

### Step 2. Creating a user

Next, create user that account and transaction data will be linked to.

Tink users can be identified either by Tink-generated `user_id` or by an `external_user_id` of your choice. 

For Connector v2 flows however, all subsequent requests (like ingesting account and transactions) will reference the user by the 'external_user_id'. This value must be kept for future reference and it also must be unique within your app. 

We recommend using a UUID format and avoiding personally identifiable information.

> **Note:** One Tink user should represent exactly one person - your end-user. If your system handles multiple end-users, you must create a separate Tink user for each of them. This ensures that all account and transaction data are logically separated and scoped to a single individual.

You will also need to provide a `market` specified as ISO 3166-1 country code that your user are in. A full reference of which markets are supported can be found [here](/resources/transactions/transactions-sdk-reference#markets.md).

**Example request:**
```bash
curl -v -X POST https://api.tink.com/api/v1/user/create \
-H 'Authorization: Bearer {YOUR_CLIENT_ACCESS_TOKEN}' \
-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
-d '{
      "external_user_id": "your_generated_uuid_user_id",
      "market": "GB" 
    }'
```

**Example response:**
```json
{
  "external_user_id": "your_generated_uuid_user_id",
  "user_id": "tink_user_id"
}
```
For more information, see complete [User documentation reference](/api-general#general/user).

### Step 3. Ingesting an account
With a user created, the next step is to create the first account for this user.

To do this, send a request to the accounts endpoint using the same `externalUserId` from Step 2 and valid Client Access Token. If your token from Step 1 has expired, generate a new one before continuing.

>**Reminder:** Client Access Tokens are valid typically for 30 minutes. If expired, generate a new one before continuing using method from Step 1.

Each account must include an unique `externalAccountId`, which you provide and manage. This identifier acts as out persistent reference to the account - you will need it when updating or deleting the account or when ingesting transactions.

>**Note:** The `externalAccountId` must be unique and immutable. You will use it for future operations related to this account, such as managing its transactions and the account itself.

**Example request**

```bash
curl -v -X POST https://api.tink.com/data/v2/connector/accounts
-H 'Authorization: Bearer {CLIENT_ACCESS_TOKEN}' \
-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
-d '{
  "accounts": [
    {
      "externalUserId": "your_generated_uuid_user_id",
      "externalAccountId": "your_generated_uuid_account_id",
      "type": "CREDIT_CARD",
      "currencyCode": "SEK"
    }  
  ]
}'
```

**Example response**
```text
200 OK
```

If the request is successful, the API respons with `200 OK` status. The response body may be empty - this indicates the account was accepted and processed successfully.

For more details how to ingest, update or delete accounts, see the full [Connector v2 Accounts API reference](#tbd).

### Step 4. Ingesting transactions

Now that you have created an account, you are ready to ingest transactions for that account.

Depending on your use case, transactions ingestion can be performed in two ways:
1. Backfilling historical transactions (eg. when onboarding a new user or syncing daily batches).
2. Ingesting real-time transactions (eg. when sending transactions shortly after they happen).

Both ingestion types use the same endpoint and structure, but differ in how they are prioritised and processed. The ingestion behaviour is determined by the value of the `operationPriorityType` in the request JSON payload.

#### Backfilling historical transactions in the background

When onboarding a new user, you often want to backfill their historical transactions in a bigger batch - for example, transactions from the past few months or years. In such cases, we recommend sending transactions batched using the `operationPriorityType` set to `BACKGROUND`. This flags the ingestion job as non-blocking and allows Tink to optimise processing and resource usage.

> **Note:** The maximum total number of transactions per request is 2,500.

You can also use this type for recurring batch updates, such as daily ingestion of transactions that occurred over the day.

#### Ingesting real-time transactions

If your use case involves ingesting transactions as they are executed - for example, sending transactions shortly after they are initiated or posted - we recommend setting the `operationPriorityType` to `REAL_TIME`.

This type is designed for small volumes of transactions and aim for high priority processing. It should be only used when the end user is actively waiting for results to be presented in your app.

#### Composing the request

After determining the `operationPriorityType`, in order to ingest transactions send a request to the Connector v2 Transactions endpoint using the same `externalUserId` and `externalAccountId`. 

Each transaction must also include an `externalTransactionId`, which you define and store. This identifier is your unique reference to the transactions and is required if you need to update or delete this transaction later.

Before sending the request, make sure to include the `Batch-Failure-Type` header to define how the batch ingestion should handle errors.
- Use `FullIngestion` to enforce strict validation. If any transaction in the batch is invalid, the entire operation will fail immediately.
- Use `PartialIngestion` to allow partial success. Valid transactions will be processed, while invalid one will be skipped and can be corrected and ingested after the operation is processed.

**Example request**

```bash
curl -v -X POST https://api.tink.com/data/v2/connector/transactions \
-H 'Authorization: Bearer {YOUR_CLIENT_ACCESS_TOKEN}' \
-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
-H 'Batch-Failure-Type: FullIngestion' \
-d '{
    "operationPriorityType": "BACKGROUND",
    "externalOperationId": "your_generated_uuid_operation_id",
    "users": [
        {
            "externalUserId": "your_generated_uuid_user_id",
            "accounts": [
                {
                    "externalAccountId": "your_generated_uuid_account_id",
                    "transactions": [
                        {
                            "externalTransactionId": "your_generated_uuid_transaction_id",
                            "amount": -98.54,
                            "descriptions": {
                                "original": "Spotify"
                            },
                            "bookedDateTime": "2024-12-15T09:25:12.132Z",
                            "status": "BOOKED",
                            "merchantInformation": {
                                "merchantCategoryCode": "4111",
                                "merchantName": "Local Transit Company",
                                "merchantNationalId": "abc1234",
                                "merchantLocation": {
                                    "geoLocation": {
                                        "latitude": 59.3345912,
                                        "longitude": 18.0632401
                                    },
                                    "address": {
                                        "street": "Vasagatan 11",
                                        "postalCode": "SE-111 20",
                                        "city": "Stockholm",
                                        "country": "SE"
                                    }
                                }
                            }
                        }
                    ]
                }
            ]
        }
    ]
}'
```

This endpoint is asynchronous. A `202 Accepted` status means the batch ingestion request has been received and queued for processing. The response includes both your `externalOperationId` and Tink-generated operationId. The operationId should be kept for future reference and it will be required in Step 5 when checking the batch ingestion operation status. 

**Example response**
```json
{
    "operationId": "0d043ee34c594d289794fae110d87bb4",
    "externalOperationId": "your_generated_uuid_operation_id"
}
```

For more information on how to ingest, update or delete transactions, please see the [Connector v2 Transactions API reference](#tba).

### Step 5. Check operation status

After submitting a transaction batch ingestion request, you can check whether the operation was completed successfully by qyerying the operation status.

Use the `operationId` returned in the response from Step 4 to track the status of the ingestion job. The status will indicate whether the operation succeeded, partially succeeded or failed - along with additional details about rejected transactions and error reasons if applicable.

**Example request**

```bash
curl -v -X GET /data/v2/connector/operations/{OPERATION_ID} \
-H 'Authorization: Bearer {YOUR_CLIENT_ACCESS_TOKEN}' \
```

**Example response**
```json
{
    "operationId": "aaaaaaaa-1111-bbbb-2222-92d05dfc6539",
    "users": [
        {
          "externalUserId": "your_external_user_id_1",
          "status": "processed",
          "exceptions": [
            {
                "externalAccountId": "your_external_account_id_1",
                "externalTransactionId": "your_external_transaction_id_1",
                "fieldPath": "user[0].transactionAccounts[0].transactions[3]",
                "reasons": [
                    {
                        "fieldName": "externalTransactionId",
                        "errorType": "VALUE_NOT_UNIQUE",
                        "message": "Provided value must be unique."
                    }
                ]
            }
          ]
        }
    ]
} 
```
The operation response includes a `status` that reflects the current state of the ingestion job. This help you determine whether the operation is still in progress.

To track the operation `status`:
- For requests with `operationPriorityType` set to `BACKGROUND`, poll the endpoint in 1 second intervals.
- For requests with `operationPriorityType` set to `REAL_TIME`, you can poll every 100 milliseconds instead.

In both cases, you should stop polling endpoint immediately once the `status` changes to either `processed` or `failed`. Avoid more frequent polling, as it may lead to rate limits. 

See the table below for a description of each of possible value:

| Operation Status     | Status Definition     |
| ---------- | ---------- |
| `processing`       | The operation is still being processed. You can poll the endpoint after 1 second for requests with `operationPriorityType` set to `BACKGROUND` or 100 milliseconds when this type was set to `REAL_TIME` and until the status change.       |
| `processed`       | The response may include an `exceptions` list with details of any transactions that were rejected from ingestions.       |
| `failed`       | The operation could not be processed. No transactions were ingested. Please inspect `exceptions` for more details.       |

If the operation fails or completes with partial success, the response will include list of `exceptions`. 

This list will contain details for each transactions that failed validation or processing. 

Each entry in the lists includes both `externalAccountId` and `externalTransactionId` or if for some reason this reference was lost, a `fieldPath` indicating the original Connector v2 requests initiating this operation. 

You can use the table below to understand the most common error types available in the operation `exceptions`. 

| Error Type     | Description     |
| ---------- | ---------- |
| `OTHER`       | Any other reason of an error.       |
| `VALUE_NOT_UNIQUE`       | Value is not unique.       |
| `EXTERNAL_USER_ID_NOT_EXIST`       | User with provided externalUserId is not created for this appId. The operation cannot attach accounts or transactions to an unknown app user.       |
| `DUPLICATED_EXTERNAL_USER_ID`       | The same externalUserId appears more than once in the request for this appId. Each externalUserId in the request must be unique.       |
| `EXTERNAL_ACCOUNTS_ID_NOT_EXIST`       | Provided externalAccountId is not found for the given externalUserId within this appId (user–account relation is missing).       |
| `DUPLICATED_EXTERNAL_ACCOUNTS_ID`       | The same externalAccountId is repeated for the same externalUserId in this appId. Each externalAccountId for given externalUserId must be unique.       |
| `NO_TRANSACTIONS_FOR_ACCOUNT`       | An externalAccountId for a user is provided with no transactions or an empty transactions array. At least one transaction is required when sending an account.       |
| `DUPLICATED_EXTERNAL_TRANSACTIONS_ID`       | Within a single account’s transactions, two or more items share the same externalTransactionId. Each externalTransactionId for given externalAccountId must be unique.       |
| `EXTERNAL_TRANSACTION_ID_ALREADY_EXIST`       | Provided externalTransactionId already exists for this account from a prior ingest.       |
| `TRANSACTION_AMOUNT_DECIMALS_WRONG`       | Transaction amount is present but provided with more than 2 decimal places.       |
| `TRANSACTION_AMOUNT_TOO_BIG`       | Transaction amount exceeds the maximum allowed absolute value for a single transaction.       |
| `MISSING_TRANSACTION_ORIGINAL_DESCRIPTION`       | Transaction descriptions.original is missing or null. It is required for every transaction.       |
| `MISSING_TRANSACTION_AMOUNT`       | Transactions amount is missing or null; A numeric amount is required for every transaction.       |
| `ANY_TRANSACTION_DATE_NOT_PROVIDED`       | None of bookedDateTime, valueDateTime, or transactionDateTime is provided. At least one date is required.       |
| `TRANSACTION_DATES_WITH_INCORRECT_FORMAT`       | One or more of bookedDateTime, valueDateTime, transactionDateTime is not in ISO 8601 format with milliseconds precision and with UTC timezone (e.g., yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ).       |
| `MCC_WITH_INCORRECT_FORMAT`       | The merchantCategoryCode is not exactly 4 digits as required by the Merchant Category Code standard (ISO 18245).      |
| `COUNTRY_CODE_WITH_INCORRECT_FORMAT`       | The countryCode is not a valid ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (two uppercase letters).      |
| `ANGULAR_DISTANCE_OUT_OF_RANGE`       | A single angular distance coordinate - latitude or longitude - is invalid: format. Latitude must be −90..90 and longitude must be −180..180; values must be decimal degrees with a dot as the decimal separator.      |
| `CUSTOM_OBJECT_KEY_NOT_CONFIGURED`       | The custom object contains a key that is not configured for this appId. Only pre-approved custom keys may be sent for this app.      |
| `CUSTOM_OBJECT_NOT_CONFIGURED`       | A custom object is provided but this appId is not configured to accept custom objects.      |

# Recategorise transactions

Source: https://docs.tink.com/resources/consumer-engagement/recategorise-transactions.md

# Recategorise transactions

You may want to recategorise transactions due to individual preferences. In this guide, we'll show you how to recategorise transactions.

## Prerequisites

1. You have created a [developer account](/resources/getting-started/set-up-your-account.md)
2. You have connected data to the Tink Platform (- we recommend using [Demo Bank](/resources/money-manager/money-manager-api/demo-banks-money-manager.md)
3. You have obtained a [user access token](/resources/money-manager/money-manager-api/access-token-money-manager.md) with the `transactions:read` scope
4. You have Money Manager enabled for your app. This can be done by contacting your Account Manager or getting in touch with [Tink Support](/resources/getting-started/support.md)
Create a developer account
5. You have the transaction ID of the transactions you want recategorise. If you don't already have them to hand, please follow step one in the [Create a list of categorised transactions](/resources/money-manager/money-manager-api/list-categorised-transactions.md) guide.

## 1. Fetch Category IDs
We first need to fetch a list of categories and their associated IDs. This can be performed by using the [list categories](/api#general/category/list-categories) endpoint while unauthenticated.

Request example:

```bash
curl 'https://api.tink.com/api/v1/categories?locale=en_US'
```

Response example:

```json
[
  {
    "code": "expenses:food.restaurants",
    "defaultChild": false,
    "id": "7e88d58188ee49749adca59e152324b6",
    "parent": "067fa4c769774ae980435c76be328c0b",
    "primaryName": "Food & Drinks",
    "searchTerms": "food,lunch,snacks",
    "secondaryName": "Restaurants",
    "sortOrder": 45,
    "type": "EXPENSES",
    "typeName": "Expenses"
  }
]
```

From the response, you can choose the category you want your transactions to belong to. Just keep note of its associated category ID for the next step.

## 2. Recategorise transaction
When you know what transactions you want to recategorise, and the category you want to change it to, you need to use the [Categorize multiple transactions](/api#data-v1/transaction/change-category-of-transactions) endpoint using a `user access token` with the `transactions:write` scope.

In the request, you need to include the `categoryId` of the category you want the transactions to belong to instead, and an array of all the transaction IDs you want the new category to apply to.

Request example:

```bash
curl 'https://api.tink.com/api/v1/transactions/categorize-multiple' \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer {USER_ACCESS_TOKEN}' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-raw '{
    "categorizationList": [
        {
            "categoryId": "{categoryId}",
            "transactionIds": [
                "{transactionId1}",
                "{transactionid2}",
                "{transactionid3}"
            ]
        },
    ]
  }'
```

Well done! You will then have successfully recategorised your transactions.

# Link transactions

Source: https://docs.tink.com/resources/consumer-engagement/link-transactions.md

# Link transactions

## Introduction
Link transactions allow the user to split their expenses and match that expense to an income, in order to not include other people's spending.

We can imagine a situation where you are going to a restaurant with a friend, and you pay the bill. Your friend sends his part of the expense back to you, and you can link it to your payment. A transaction part is then made, and your spending is decreased with the linked transaction amount. You will then have a clear view of your real spending.

[Here](/api#data-v1/transaction/link-transactions) you can find more technical information about linking transactions.

Example request:

```bash
curl 'https://api.tink.com/api/v1/transactions/{id}/link/{counterpartTransactionId}' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer {YOUR_USER_ACCESS_TOKEN}' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-raw '{
    "amount": 125
  }'
```

where:

| Element                    | Required | Description                                                                                                                           |
|----------------------------|----------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `id`                       | yes      | ID of your transaction (expense at the restaurant)                                                                                    |
| `counterpartTransactionId` | yes      | ID of transaction including your friends part of the spending                                                                         |
| `amount`                   | no       | Transaction link amount. Required to have the same sign as transaction. When not specified the common disposable amount will be used. |

Example response (incomplete):

```json
{
    "transaction": {
        "id": "0f0074bdda9b49baa960a5eb405a8b3d",
        "amount": -550.0,
        "categoryType": "EXPENSES",
        "parts": [
            {
                "id": "adbaa14742b248e49d05ebeb92936c47",
                "counterpartTransactionId": "45e7750579904dcc8c7036cbc1cbde61",
                "counterpartDescription": "Link_2",
                "amount": -125.0,
                "counterpartTransactionAmount": 125.0
            }
        ],
        "dispensableAmount": -425.0
    },
    "counterpartTransaction": {
        "id": "45e7750579904dcc8c7036cbc1cbde61",
        "amount": 125.0,
        "categoryType": "INCOME",
        "parts": [
            {
                "id": "6e14820603b1470f980df94f3fba7ddb",
                "counterpartTransactionId": "0f0074bdda9b49baa960a5eb405a8b3d",
                "counterpartDescription": "Link_1",
                "amount": 125.0,
                "counterpartTransactionAmount": -550.0
            }
        ],
        "dispensableAmount": 0
    }
}
```

# Create a list of categorised transactions

Source: https://docs.tink.com/resources/consumer-engagement/list-categorised-transactions.md

# Create a list of categorised transactions

This article will help you get started with Money Manager by fetching a list of categorised transactions.


## Prerequisites

1. You have created a [developer account](/resources/getting-started/set-up-your-account.md)
2. You have connected data to the Tink Platform (- we recommend using [Demo Bank](/resources/money-manager/money-manager-api/demo-banks-money-manager.md) while testing)
3. You have obtained a [user access token](/resources/money-manager/money-manager-api/access-token-money-manager.md) with the `transactions:read` scope
4. You have Money Manager enabled for your app. This can be done by contacting your Account Manager or getting in touch with [Tink Support](/resources/getting-started/support.md)

We will show you how to fetch a user's latest transactions. It will be sorted by date, including a cleaned transaction description, amount, currency and category. This can be used to help your end users get a quick overview of all their accounts from different providers and see transactions in one single place.

## 1. List transactions
To fetch a user's transactions, you need to use the [Search endpoint](/api#data-v1/search). As part of the API call, you also need to include a `user access token` with the `transactions:read` scope. A detailed description of the API and its capabilities can be found [here](/api#data-v1/search).

In this example, we will use dates as the main query parameter to list all possible transactions during the last three months. In the response, you will get an ordered list of transactions with details.

Example request:

```bash
curl 'https://api.tink.com/api/v1/search' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer {YOUR_USER_ACCESS_TOKEN}' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-raw '{
    "endDate": "{CURRENT_DATE}",
    "includeUpcoming": false,
    "order": "ASC",
    "sort": "DATE",
    "startDate": "{CURRENT_DATE-3_months}"
  }'
```

Example response:

```json
{
  "count": 110,
  "metrics": {
    "AVG": 15.0,
    "COUNT": 110,
    "NET": 1288.45,
    "SUM": 1650.0
  },
  "net": 1288.45,
  "periodAmounts": [
    {
      "key": "string",
      "value": 0
    }
  ],
  "query": {
  "endDate": {CURRENT DATE),
  "includeUpcoming": false,
  "order": "ASC",
  "sort": "DATE",
  "startDate": {CURRENT DATE-3 months)
},
  "results": [
    {
      "transaction": {
        "accountId": "3fe2d96efacd4dc5994404a950f238a9",
        "amount": 34.5,
        "categoryId": "0e1bade6a7e3459eb794f27b7ba4cea0",
        "categoryType": "EXPENSES",
        "currencyDenominatedAmount": {
          "currencyCode": "EUR",
          "scale": 2,
          "unscaledValue": 1050
        },
        "currencyDenominatedOriginalAmount": {
          "currencyCode": "EUR",
          "scale": 2,
          "unscaledValue": 1050
        },
        "date": 1455740874875,
        "description": "H&M",
        "dispensableAmount": 0,
        "id": "79c6c9c27d6e42489e888e08d27205a1",
        "identifiers": {
          "providerExternalId": "string"
        },
        "lastModified": 1455740874875,
        "notes": "Delicious #cake #wedding",
        "originalAmount": 34.5,
        "originalDate": 1455740874875,
        "originalDescription": "Stadium Sergelg Stockholm",
        "partnerPayload": {},
        "parts": [
          {
            "amount": 34.5,
            "categoryId": "0e1bade6a7e3459eb794f27b7ba4cea0",
            "counterpartDescription": "Stadium Sergelg Stockholm",
            "counterpartId": "79c6c9c27d6e42489e888e08d27205a1",
            "counterpartTransactionAmount": 10.0,
            "counterpartTransactionId": "d030a7b0840547428aa2fd07026e9a77",
            "date": 1455740874875,
            "id": "7303ff128531463bbed358bbf9e23f31",
            "lastModified": 1455740874875
          }
        ],
        "payload": {},
        "pending": false,
        "timestamp": 1464543093494,
        "type": "CREDIT_CARD",
        "upcoming": false,
        "userId": "d9f134ee2eb44846a4e02990ecc8d32e",
        "userModified": false
      },
      "type": "TRANSACTION"
    }
  ]
}
```

As part of the API response, you'll be returned multiple fields of data. However for this walkthrough, we’re only interested in the following:

| Field          | Description                                                                |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `amount`       | The category of the transaction                                            |
| `categoryType` | The category type of the transaction. Values: INCOME, EXPENSES, TRANSFERS  |
| `date`         | The date the transaction was executed                                      |
| `description`  | The cleaned description of the transaction                                 |
| `currencyCode` | The ISO 4217 currency code of the transaction                              |

Filter on the fields above and you have a simple list of the users' latest transactions. The only thing that’s missing now is to replace the category IDs with human readable category names.

## 2. Fetch category names
You then need to fetch a list of available categories to match up against the category IDs you received from the search endpoint. This is achieved by using the [list categories](/api#general/category/list-categories) endpoint when unauthenticated.

Example request:

```bash
curl 'https://api.tink.com/api/v1/categories?locale=en_US'
```

Example response:

```json
[
  {
    "code": "expenses:food.restaurants",
    "defaultChild": false,
    "id": "7e88d58188ee49749adca59e152324b6",
    "parent": "067fa4c769774ae980435c76be328c0b",
    "primaryName": "Food & Drinks",
    "searchTerms": "food,lunch,snacks",
    "secondaryName": "Restaurants",
    "sortOrder": 45,
    "type": "EXPENSES",
    "typeName": "Expenses"
  }
]
```

From this response, you'll need the following parameters:

| Parameter       | Description                                                               |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`            | The internal identifier of the category, referenced by e.g. a transaction |
| `primaryName`   | The primary name of this category                                         |
| `secondaryName` | The secondary name of this category                                       |

You are now able to match the ID from the [List categories](/api#general/category/list-categories) response and `categoryId` from the [Search](/api#data-v1/search) response to derive the category name.

> **Note**: Primary name is the top level category name (e.g. Food & Drinks), while the secondary name is the subcategory level name (e.g. Restaurant). You can choose to present either to the end-user or use your own wording.

With this, you will be able to present a list of transactions ordered by date, with a clean readable description and category to the end-user.

# Get data into the Tink platform using Aggregation

Source: https://docs.tink.com/resources/consumer-engagement/get-data-into-the-tink-platform-using-aggregation.md

# Get data into the Tink platform using Aggregation

## Prerequisites

Configuring your application to use Data Enrichment, see article [here](/resources/data-enrichment/configure-your-application-to-use-data-enrichment.md).

Almost all endpoints that are used by Data Enrichment require permanent users and end-user transaction data. There are two methods to get a user’s transactions to the platform: through Aggregation (which delegates the task of transaction ingestion to Tink if an end-user has given consent) or through manual ingestion by using the Connector API. Select the approach that fits your use case. The aggregation method is presented below. For more information about the manual ingestion by using the Connector API, see [link](/resources/data-enrichment/get-data-into-the-tink-platform-using-the-connector.md).

## Aggregation

Aggregation is a process where your end users grant Tink permission to aggregate their accounts and transactions to the Tink platform. This is done through Tink Link, Tink’s front-end SDK for end-user authentication. Using Tink Link, you have access to a ready-made authentication flow by only using a single line of code, for any bank or market.

Aggregation can be done using temporary or permanent users. Temporary users are deleted after 24 hours. For Data Enrichment, permanent users are required. See configuring your application to use Data Enrichment to make sure that everything is set up properly.

This article guides you through steps to create a permanent Tink user and then using Tink Link to aggregate end-user data to that user. The data is then continuously updated without end-user interactions on a time interval that is dependent on a selected bank/provider.

There are caveats to some of these steps and every possible scenario won’t be covered in this article. We encourage you to read the full API references linked throughout the guide if you intend to use this in production.

The steps in this guide:
1. Create a client access token
2. Create a user
3. Create a delegated client code
4. Create a Tink URL
5. Redirect a user through the generated Tink Link URL
6. Managing user consent

### Step 1: Create a client access token

The following request authorizes the application by using the client id/secret and requesting a client access token with the user:create and authorization:grant scope permissions. The client access token grants your application access to all endpoints needed for aggregation. The token is valid for 30 minutes.

__Example request:__

```bash
curl -v -X POST https://api.tink.com/api/v1/oauth/token \
-d 'client_id={YOUR_CLIENT_ID}' \
-d 'client_secret={YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET}' \
-d 'grant_type=client_credentials' \
-d 'scope=user:create,authorization:grant'
```

__Example response:__

```json
  "access_token": "{YOUR_CLIENT_ACCESS_TOKEN}",
  "token_type": "bearer",
  "expires_in": 1800,
  "scope": "user:create,authorization:grant"
```

For more information, see [complete documentation reference](https://docs.tink.com/api#general/oauth/get-access-token "Get access token").

### Step 2: Create a user

Use the generated client access token from step 1 to create a new Tink user. Attach and store a unique external user ID to keep a reference to the user. The external user ID is used in later steps. Also add the code for the market that you wish to use.  For a list of market codes, see [Markets](/resources/transactions/transactions-sdk-reference#markets "Markets".md).

__Example request:__
```bash
curl -v -X POST https://api.tink.com/api/v1/user/create \
-H 'Authorization: Bearer {YOUR_CLIENT_ACCESS_TOKEN}' \
-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
-d '
    {
      "external_user_id": "user_123_abc",
      "market": "GB", 
    }
  '
````

__Example response:__
```json
{
  "external_user_id": "user_123_abc",
  "user_id": "THE_CREATED_USER_ID"
}
```

For more information, see [complete documentation reference](https://docs.tink.com/api#general/user/create-user "Create user").

### Step 3: Create a delegated client code

Use the generated client access token from step 1 and the external user ID from step 2 to create a delegated client code. This code is used by Tink Link to act on behalf of your application (to ingest end-user data to your Tink application, for example). Some additional fields also needs to be specified: 

|      |      |
| ---------- | ---------- |
| external_user_id       | The external user ID of the Tink user that should be connected to the end-user’s data       |
| actor_client_id       | The ID of the actor client that is allowed to use the delegated client token we generate in step 3 (this step). In this case, the actor client is Tink Link, and the field should be hard coded to ‘df05e4b379934cd09963197cc855bfe9', which is the client ID for TInk Link.        |
| id_hint       | This is presented to the end-user in the Tink Link flow. You can use any arbitrary string value that is recognizable to the end user, such as the end user's full name or email address. id_hint is used to verify the identity of the user and to prevent URL spoofing attacks.       |
| scope       | The scopes that are granted to Tink Link within your application. The scopes present in the example is what is needed for aggregation.       |

__Example request:__
```bash
curl -v -X POST https://api.tink.com/api/v1/oauth/authorization-grant/delegate \
-H 'Authorization: Bearer {YOUR_CLIENT_ACCESS_TOKEN}' \
-d 'external_user_id={EXTERNAL_USER_ID_CREATED_ABOVE}'\
-d 'actor_client_id=df05e4b379934cd09963197cc855bfe9' \
-d 'id_hint={End user name/username}\
-d 'scope=authorization:read,authorization:grant,credentials:refresh,credentials:read,credentials:write,providers:read,user:read'
````

__Example response:__
```json
{
  "code": "{DELEGATED_CLIENT_CODE}"
}
````

For more information, see [complete documentation reference](https://docs.tink.com/api#general/user/create-user "Create user").

### Step 4: Create a Tink Link URL

In this step we’re going to construct the Tink Link URL by using the delegated client code that was created in step 3. The URL can be broken into three parts: a base URL, an endpoint, and a set of query parameters that configures the URL. 

In this article we focus on the minimal amount of query parameters that are needed to configure the Tink Link URL for aggregation. 

Here’s an example Tink Link URL: 

`https://link.tink.com/1.0/transactions/connect-accounts?authorization_code={DELEGATED_CLIENT_CODE}&client_id={YOUR_CLIENT_ID}&redirect_uri={REDIRECT_URI}&market={MARKET}&locale={LOCALE}`

To break down the URL, we have the base URL, https://link.tink.com/1.0/,
followed by a specific endpoint for transaction and account aggregation, transactions/connect-accounts, followed by the minimal set of query parameters:

| Header     | Header     |
| ---------- | ---------- |
| authorization_code       | The delegated client code generated in step 3. It encodes the reference to the user as well as the scopes that are granted to the Tink Link URL.       |
| client_id       | The client ID of your application. ​​To see your client ID, open Console and go to [your_app] > App settings > API Client.       |
| redirect_uri       | The URL to which the end user gets redirected after a completed or failed authentication by the end user.       |
| market       | Market/country code for which providers/banks should be available for the end user to authenticate towards/aggregate data. For example, GB for Great Britain. For a list of market codes, see [Markets](/resources/transactions/transactions-sdk-reference#markets "Markets".md).       |
| locale       | Locale for end-user facing text. For example, en_US for English. For a list of locale codes, see [Locales](/resources/transactions/transactions-sdk-reference#locales "Locales".md).       |

For more information, see [complete documentation reference](/resources/transactions/transactions-sdk-reference#continuous-access-connect-accounts "Continuous access connect accounts".md).

### Step 5: Redirect a user through the generated Tink Link URL

How to do this varies depending on if you’re building a web, Android, or iOS application. In a web application a simple:  window.location.replace `{YOUR_GENERATED_TINK_LINK_URL}` could suffice.

When end users access a Tink Link URL, through the web browser or an iOS/Android SDK implementation, they will see a list of banks/providers. Once they select a bank/provider they will be forwarded to that specific bank/provider’s authentication flow. When the authentication flow is completed, both for successes and failures, the end user is redirected to the redirect URL that’s specified in the Tink Link URL query parameters.

Meanwhile, in the background, if the authentication was successful, the user’s transactions and selected accounts will be aggregated into Tink’s platform and connected to the Tink user encoded in the authorization_code.

!https://images.ctfassets.net/tmqu5vj33f7w/4dTo01RRCA15Ay8mhfishU/1b28225dad3e8aba96bb113740c8a005/transactions-flow-example.gif

Depending if the authentication was successful or not, Tink Link will append a set of different query parameters to the redirect URL for you to handle. In this guide, we will focus on what happens on a successful authentication attempt. Take a look at our complete documentation reference to see all possible outcomes.

On success, the your redirect URL will be called as follows:

    {REDIRECT_URL}?credentials_id={ID} 

The credentials_id is a reference to the consent that the end-user has given. The consent is also an object that’s connected to the user stored on the Tink Platform which must be updated over time. The next section will briefly cover consents, but if you just want to aggregate data to try it out, you can end the guide here.

To double-check that the data has been aggregated correctly, see the generating a user token and querying end-user data article.

### Step 6: Manage user consent
Because of data regulations, user consent is not valid forever. To keep refreshing data in the background, the consent will need to be updated over time. How often the consent needs to be updated is dependent on which bank/provider the end-user has authenticated. 

Update the consent by going through the same process as in steps 2-3, but with a slightly different Tink Link URL:

    https://link.tink.com/1.0/transactions/update-consent?authorization_code={code}&client_id={id}&redirect_uri={uriI}&credentials_id={id}

The difference between this and the previous URL that you set up in step 4 is that the endpoint has changed to `transactions/update-consent` and we’ve added the credential_id parameter. More query parameters can be used to configure the URL, take a look here if you are interested.

You can keep track of a user’s consents either by querying the consent endpoints, or by setting up webhooks, see the following references:
- [Managing user consents](/resources/transactions/managing-consents.md)
- [Provider consent API docs](https://docs.tink.com/api#connectivity/provider-consent/list-provider-consents)
- [Setting up webhooks for your application](/resources/api-setup/webhooks.md)

---

# Find similar transactions

This guide will show you how to create a list of similar transactions.


## Prerequisites

1. You have created a [developer account](/resources/getting-started/set-up-your-account.md)
2. You have connected data to the Tink Platform (- we recommend using [Demo Bank](/resources/money-manager/money-manager-api/demo-banks-money-manager.md)
3. You have obtained a [user access token](/resources/money-manager/money-manager-api/access-token-money-manager.md) with the `transactions:read` scope
4. You have Money Manager enabled for your app. This can be done by contacting your Account Manager or getting in touch with [Tink Support](/resources/getting-started/support.md)


There may be occasions where you want to retrieve a list of similar transactions. For instance in a PFM app setting, you may want to see all of the similar groceries transactions to allow a user to quickly see the different transactions along with statistics. Or when you're looking to recategorise transactions and you want to recategorise all the similar transactions.

To get started, you need to use the [Get similar transaction](/api#data-v1/transaction/get-similar-transactions) endpoint. To use this endpoint, you need to also provide a `user access token` with the `transactions:read` scope. In the request, you need to also include the transaction ID of the transaction you want to find similar transactions for.

As part of the request, the parameters give you the option to return similar transactions which belong to a category (rather than ones with a similar description) if you provide the `categoryId`. You can also choose to include the same transaction in the response. For the purpose of this guide, we will not fetch similar transactions based on the category, we will instead include the same transactions in response.

Example request:

```bash
curl 'https://api.tink.com/api/v1/transactions/{transactionId}/similar?includeSelf=true'
```

```json
      },

      "formattedDescription": "Stadium Sergelgatan Stockholm",
      "id": "79c6c9c27d6e42489e888e08d27205a1",
      "inserted": 1455740874875,
      "lastModified": 1455740874875,
      "notes": "Delicious #cake #wedding",
      "originalAmount": 34.5,
```

**NOTE**: When you have a list of similar transactions and their associated IDs, you may want to recategorise some of them at the same time. If so, please follow this [guide](/resources/money-manager/money-manager-api/recategorise-transactions.md) for guidance.
